Fleck 5600 is not responding, what are troubleshooting steps?

raw_model_output:
For troubleshooting a Fleck 5600 water softener that is not responding, the following steps are recommended:

- Check for electrical service interruptions to the unit. Ensure permanent electrical service by checking the fuse, plug, pull chain, or switch.
- Verify that the timer is functioning properly. If defective, replace the timer.
- Inspect the powerhead and control components for any faults.
- Check for foreign material in the control by removing the power head assembly and inspecting the bore. Remove any foreign material found.
- Examine the drive motor and switches to ensure they are operating correctly.
- If the control cycles continuously, determine if a switch or timer is faulty and replace it or replace the complete power head.
- Check for internal control leaks and replace seals, spacers, and piston assembly if necessary.
- Clean plugged components such as the drain line flow control, injector, and injector screen.
- Verify that the line pressure is adequate (increase to 20 psi if too low).
- Ensure the valve is programming correctly by checking the timer program and positioning of the control. Replace the power head assembly if it is not positioning properly.
- If the drain flows continuously, check the valve programming and control positioning.
- For any issues related to the piston or control bore, remove the piston and clean the control.

These steps are compiled from the troubleshooting guidance for the Fleck 5600SXT Upflow and Downflow service manuals and cover common causes and corrections for a non-responding unit. [Document 4, p.20]

18 • F LECK 5800/5810/5812 XTRi Service Manual 
PENTAIR PRO: APP SETUP 
Pairing the Fleck  5800/5810/5812 XTRi Con­nected 
Valve with Wi-Fi Devices 
The Fleck  5800/5810/5812 XTRi Connected Valve can be paired 
with a smartphone or tablet. New users can download and install 
the Pentair Home App from the App Store or Google Play. WiFi 
connection must be 2.4 GHz.
Sign Up and Log In 
New users will need to create an account to monitor their water 
softeners. From the Log In page, press SIGN UP to create a new 
account. If you already have an account, skip to Login.
 Add your email address and set your password.
Once you select Create Account, an email will be sent to your 
email for verification.
 Click the “Verify Email” link to complete the process.

PTFE plumbing tape is the only sealant to be used on the drain fitting. 8. Make sure that the floor is clean beneath the salt storage tank and that the tank is level.
9.	 Place approximately 1" (25 mm) of water above the grid
plate. If a grid is not utilized, fill to the top of the air check
(Figure 1) in the salt tank. Do not add salt to the brine tank
at this time.
CAUTION  If grid plate is used, cut air check height even with
grid plate. This is critical on 6", 7", 8" and 9" tanks.
The brine refill water must come above the grid
plate and make contact with the salt.
10.	On units with a bypass, place in bypass position. Turn on
the main water supply. Open a cold soft water tap nearby
and let run a few minutes or until the plumbing is free from
foreign material (usually solder) that may have resulted
from the installation. Once clean, close the water tap.
11.	Slowly place the bypass in service position and let water
flow into the mineral tank. When water flow stops, slowly
open a cold water tap nearby and let water run until the air
is purged from the plumbing lines.
12.	Plug the transformer into an electrical outlet.
NOTE:  	All electrical connections must be connected
according to local codes. Be certain the outlet is
uninterrupted.

To install the Fleck 5600SXT, follow these steps:

1. Ensure that the floor beneath the salt storage tank is clean and level.
2. Place approximately 1 inch (25 mm) of water above the grid plate in the salt tank. If a grid is not used, fill to the top of the air check in the salt tank. Do not add salt at this time.
3. If a grid plate is used, cut the air check height even with the grid plate. This is critical for 6", 7", 8", and 9" tanks. The brine refill water must come above the grid plate and make contact with the salt.
4. On units with a bypass, place the bypass in the bypass position.
5. Turn on the main water supply.
6. Open a cold soft water tap nearby and let it run for a few minutes or until the plumbing is free from foreign material (usually solder) that may have resulted from the installation. Once clean, close the water tap.
7. Slowly place the bypass in the service position and let water flow into the mineral tank.
8. When water flow stops, slowly open a cold water tap nearby and let water run until the air is purged from the plumbing lines.
9. Plug the transformer into an electrical outlet. Ensure all electrical connections comply with local codes and that the outlet is uninterrupted.

Note: Use PTFE plumbing tape as the only sealant on the drain fitting, and be careful with solder joints to avoid interior damage to the DLFC (Drain Line Flow Control).

Install MAG 5000 / MAG 6000 compact version 
1. Remove and discard terminal box lid of sensor. 
 
2. Ensure SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed. 
3. Fit M20 or ½" NPT cable glands for supply and output cables. 
4. Unplug the two black plug assemblies for coil and electrode cables in terminal box.

6. Connect 2-pin connector and 3-pin connector as shown to their corresponding terminal 
numbers on connection board as shown in Electrical connection (Page 36).

TIMER OPERATION
Meter Immediate Control
A meter immediate control measures water usage and
regenerates the system as soon as the calculated system
capacity is depleted. The control calculates the system
capacity by dividing the unit capacity (typically expressed in
grains/unit volume) by the feedwater hardness and subtracting
the reserve. Meter Immediate systems generally do not use a
reserve volume. However, in twin tank systems with soft-water
regeneration, the reserve capacity should be set to the volume
of water used during regeneration to prevent hard water
break-through. A Meter Immediate control will also start a
regeneration cycle at the programmed regeneration time if a
number of days equal to the regeneration day override pass
before water usage depletes the calculated system capacity.
Meter Delayed Control
A Meter Delayed Control measures water usage and
regenerates the system at the programmed regeneration time
after the calculated system capacity is depleted. As with Meter
Immediate systems, the control calculates the system capacity
by dividing the unit capacity by the feedwater hardness and
subtracting the reserve. The reserve should be set to insure
that the system delivers treated water between the time the
system capacity is depleted and the actual regeneration time.
A Meter Delayed control will also start a regeneration cycle at
the programmed regeneration time if a number of days equal
to the regeneration day override pass before water usage
depletes the calculated system capacity.

of residences with a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m). The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m). Because the system is pressurized, the number of floors in a home is not taken into consideration
in sizing the circulating pump. The pump has only to produce continuous flow at a pressure
sufficient to overcome the friction losses created by the piping in the house water supply line
and the return line.
NOTICE: Water pressure
A recirculating system is a pressurized system operating at the city water pressure, as
determined by the pressure regulator on your line, or by a well pump, if you are on a well system.
In most residential plumbing systems, water pressure is set at 35 psi (241 kPa) and above.
Below 35 psi (241 kPa), water pressure may not be sufficient to fill the pipe diameter, leaving
space for air to accumulate in the lines.
If your system pressure is less than 35 psi (241 kPa), use the next larger pump on the Pump
Selection Guide.
NOTICE: Oversized pumps
Pumps should not be so large as to produce flow rates that may eventually erode holes in the
pipes. According to the Copper Development Association, excessive erosion occurs at a velocity
of about 5 ft (1.5 m) per second and higher; or about 4 gpm (15 l/min) in 1/2" Type M copper
pipe.
Use the recommended recirculation line size shown in the Pump Selection Guide. The e3 series
pumps are sized so that flow velocities are below these limits.

of residences with a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m). The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m). Because the system is pressurized, the number of floors in a home is not taken into consideration
in sizing the circulating pump. The pump has only to produce continuous flow at a pressure
sufficient to overcome the friction losses created by the piping in the house water supply line
and the return line.
NOTICE: Water pressure
A recirculating system is a pressurized system operating at the city water pressure, as
determined by the pressure regulator on your line, or by a well pump, if you are on a well system.
In most residential plumbing systems, water pressure is set at 35 psi (241 kPa) and above.
Below 35 psi (241 kPa), water pressure may not be sufficient to fill the pipe diameter, leaving
space for air to accumulate in the lines.
If your system pressure is less than 35 psi (241 kPa), use the next larger pump on the Pump
Selection Guide.
NOTICE: Oversized pumps
Pumps should not be so large as to produce flow rates that may eventually erode holes in the
pipes. According to the Copper Development Association, excessive erosion occurs at a velocity
of about 5 ft (1.5 m) per second and higher; or about 4 gpm (15 l/min) in 1/2" Type M copper
pipe.
Use the recommended recirculation line size shown in the Pump Selection Guide. The e3 series
pumps are sized so that flow velocities are below these limits.

[pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4]
4 • FLECK 7000SXT Service Manual
INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

TIMER OPERATION
Meter Immediate Control
A meter immediate control measures water usage and
regenerates the system as soon as the calculated system
capacity is depleted. The control calculates the system
capacity by dividing the unit capacity (typically expressed in
grains/unit volume) by the feedwater hardness and subtracting
the reserve. Meter Immediate systems generally do not use a
reserve volume. However, in twin tank systems with soft-water
regeneration, the reserve capacity should be set to the volume
of water used during regeneration to prevent hard water
break-through. A Meter Immediate control will also start a
regeneration cycle at the programmed regeneration time if a
number of days equal to the regeneration day override pass
before water usage depletes the calculated system capacity.
Meter Delayed Control
A Meter Delayed Control measures water usage and
regenerates the system at the programmed regeneration time
after the calculated system capacity is depleted. As with Meter
Immediate systems, the control calculates the system capacity
by dividing the unit capacity by the feedwater hardness and
subtracting the reserve. The reserve should be set to insure
that the system delivers treated water between the time the
system capacity is depleted and the actual regeneration time.
A Meter Delayed control will also start a regeneration cycle at
the programmed regeneration time if a number of days equal
to the regeneration day override pass before water usage
depletes the calculated system capacity.
Time Clock Delayed Control

Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.

voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.

water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.

making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.

10. Verify that the pump is not experiencing low water level or static lift issues.
11. Check for any mechanical failures or misalignment.

Service Instructions (Cont’d.)
Seal and Spacer Replacement
To replace seals and spacers, refer to Replacing Brine Valve, Injectors and Screen, steps 1–3.
1.
Remove the control valve back cover. Remove the control valve front cover. Disconnect the meter dome signal wire from
the front cover and feed it back through the control.
2.
Remove screw and washer at drive yoke. Remove timer mounting screws. The entire timer assembly will now lift off
easily. Remove end plug retainer plate.
3.
Pull upward on end of piston rod yoke until assembly is out of valve. Remove and replace seals and spacers.
4.
Take piston assembly and push piston into valve by means of the end plug. Twist yoke carefully in a clockwise direction
to properly align it with drive gear. Replace end plug retainer plate.
5.
Place timer on top of valve. Be sure drive pin on main gear engages slot in drive yoke.
6.
Replace timer mounting screws. Replace screw and washer at drive yoke.
7.
Return bypass or inlet valving to normal In Service position. Water pressure automatically builds in the conditioner.
NOTE: Be sure to shut off any bypass line.
8.
Replace the control valve back cover.
9.
Follow Injectors/Screen Replacement, steps 9–12.
Meter Replacement
To replace meter refer to Replacing Brine Valve, Injectors and Screen, steps 1–3.
1.
Remove two screws and clips at bypass valve or yoke. Pull resin tank away from plumbing connections.
2.
Pull meter module out of control valve.
3.

TIMER OPERATION
Meter Immediate Control
A meter immediate control measures water usage and
regenerates the system as soon as the calculated system
capacity is depleted. The control calculates the system
capacity by dividing the unit capacity (typically expressed in
grains/unit volume) by the feedwater hardness and subtracting
the reserve. Meter Immediate systems generally do not use a
reserve volume. However, in twin tank systems with soft-water
regeneration, the reserve capacity should be set to the volume
of water used during regeneration to prevent hard water
break-through. A Meter Immediate control will also start a
regeneration cycle at the programmed regeneration time if a
number of days equal to the regeneration day override pass
before water usage depletes the calculated system capacity.
Meter Delayed Control
A Meter Delayed Control measures water usage and
regenerates the system at the programmed regeneration time
after the calculated system capacity is depleted. As with Meter
Immediate systems, the control calculates the system capacity
by dividing the unit capacity by the feedwater hardness and
subtracting the reserve. The reserve should be set to insure
that the system delivers treated water between the time the
system capacity is depleted and the actual regeneration time.
A Meter Delayed control will also start a regeneration cycle at
the programmed regeneration time if a number of days equal
to the regeneration day override pass before water usage
depletes the calculated system capacity.

4 • FLECK 7000SXT Service Manual
INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

Output 
● When choosing hot water, changing the output settings is not allowed and the output 
setting menus are not shown in display. 
● When choosing cold water or other liquids, all output settings can be changed. 
7.7 
MAG 6000 SV 
Excitation frequency 
The MAG 6000 SV excitation frequency can be changed in sensor characteristics menu to 
one of the following frequencies: 
● 1 9/16 Hz 
● 3 1/8 Hz 
● 6 ¼ Hz 
● 12½ Hz 
● 25 Hz 
● 44 Hz 
 
Note 
Calibration has been made with the frequency stored in SENSORPROM® memory unit. A 
change in excitation frequency is not recommended and will always mean decreased 
measuring accuracy. In some instances, however, it may be necessary to change 
frequency due to pulsating flow from piston pumps or other resonance frequencies from 
surroundings. 
It is highly recommended to carry out a External input (Page 49) after changing the excitation 
frequency as the offset is affected by the frequency selected. When this is done, the 
decrease in measuring accuracy can be kept below 1% o.r. 
A too high frequency for the sensor used will cause a coil current alarm indication.

Excitation frequency 
The MAG 6000 SV excitation frequency can be changed in sensor characteristics menu to 
one of the following frequencies: 
● 1 9/16 Hz 
● 3 1/8 Hz 
● 6 ¼ Hz 
● 12½ Hz 
● 25 Hz 
● 44 Hz 
 
Note 
Calibration has been made with the frequency stored in SENSORPROM® memory unit. A 
change in excitation frequency is not recommended and will always mean decreased 
measuring accuracy. In some instances, however, it may be necessary to change 
frequency due to pulsating flow from piston pumps or other resonance frequencies from 
surroundings. 
It is highly recommended to carry out a External input (Page 49) after changing the excitation 
frequency as the offset is affected by the frequency selected. When this is done, the 
decrease in measuring accuracy can be kept below 1% o.r.

final_context_preview:
[pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=3|s=Page 3]
FLECK
® 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual • 3
INSTALLATION & START-UP
Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
CAUTION  	Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to
freezing conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit.
NOTE:  	Be sure the tank is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve
to room temperature before operating.
3.	 Perform all plumbing according to local plumbing codes.
•	Use a 1/2-inch minimum pipe size for the drain.
•	Use a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates that
exceed 7 gpm or length that exceeds 20 feet (6 m).

START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

8. Electrical facilities must provide an uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply compatible with the unit's voltage.
9. Existing plumbing should be free from lime and iron buildup; replace piping if heavily built up or install a separate iron filter unit ahead of the water softener if clogged with iron.
10. Follow the start-up instructions to manually advance the valve through regeneration steps, including backwash, brine/slow rinse, rapid rinse, and brine tank fill cycles.

Additional cautions include not subjecting the unit to freezing conditions and not exceeding water temperature of 110°F (43°C) during installation and operation.

These steps ensure proper installation and operation of the Fleck 7000SXT water softener system. [p=4|s=Page 4], [p=5|s=Page 5]

The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the

need to be repeated).

Bell & Gossett e3-6 shows low pressure, what could cause this?

raw_model_output:
The Bell & Gossett e3-6 showing low pressure could be caused by several issues similar to those listed for deep well turbine pumps experiencing "Not enough pressure" or "Not enough liquid." Possible causes include:

- Insufficient liquid supply or cavitation due to low NPSH (Net Positive Suction Head) available. It may be necessary to lower the bowl assembly by adding a column to increase liquid supply.  
- Impellers adjusted too high, which can affect pressure output.  
- Air or gas in the water, which can be addressed by lowering the pump if possible or closing the discharge valve to maintain the well pumping level at a lower GPM.  
- Excessive pump wear, which would require pulling the pump and repairing as needed.  
- Other mechanical failures such as misalignment or clogged suction strainer could also reduce pressure.  

These causes and remedies are detailed in the troubleshooting sections for deep well turbine pumps and can be applied to similar pump issues like the Bell & Gossett e3-6 showing low pressure [xylem_goulds_water_technology_dwt_iom_deep_well_turbine_pumps_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=22|s=Page 22].

[pentair_fleck_sxt_owners_manual_fleck_sxt_controllers_owner_s_manual.pdf|p=6|s=Page 6]
to indicate a power interruption. Press the Extra Cycle button to resume normal operation. The control will not start a new regeneration cycle without line power. If the valve misses a scheduled regeneration due to a power failure, it will queue a regeneration. Once power is restored, the control will initiate a regeneration cycle the next time that the Time of Day equals the programmed regeneration time.
Typically, this means that the valve will regenerate one day after it was originally scheduled. If the treated
water output is important and power interruptions are expected, the system should be setup with a sufficient
reserve capacity to compensate for regeneration delays.
CARE AND USE OF YOUR BRINE TANK
Each time the softener regenerates, salty water (brine) is needed to recondition the media in the water tank.
The brine is pulled from the salt tank at a controlled amount. If the salt tank does not contain enough salt, the
brine is weak, the media will not fully recondition and untreated water will pass through. To ensure the highest
level of performance of your water conditioning system, please observe the following:
•	 Keep the brine tank filled with salt at all times. The salt level should always be higher than the water level
in the brine tank.
•	 Only use sodium chloride salt designed for water softeners. Other types of salt (rock or snow melting)
may contain dirt and chemicals that will affect the quality of your water and the performance of your
water softener.
•	 Keep the brine tank covered.
•	 Empty and clean the tank every three years.

SETTING TIME OF DAY AND
INITIATING A MANUAL
REGENERATION
Setting the Time of Day
1.	 Press and hold either the Up or Down buttons until
the programming icon replaces the service icon and
the parameter display reads TD.
2.	 Adjust the displayed time with the Up and Down
buttons.
3.	 When the desired time is set, press the Extra Cycle
button to resume normal operation. The unit will
also return to normal operation after five seconds if
no buttons are pressed.
Queueing a Regeneration
1.	 Press the Extra Cycle button. The service icon will
flash to indicate that a regeneration is queued.
2.	 To cancel a queued regeneration, press the Extra
Cycle button.
Regenerating Immediately
Press and hold the Extra Cycle button for five seconds.
FEATURES OF THE PENTAIR FLECK SXT CONTROLLER
•	 Power backup that continues to keep time and the passage of days for a minimum of 8 hours in the event
of power failure. During a power outage, the control goes into a power-saving mode. It does not monitor
water usage during a power failure, but it does store the volume remaining at the time of power failure.
•	 Settings for both valve (basic system) and control type (method used to trigger a regeneration).
•	 Day-of-the-Week controls.
•	 While in service, the display alternates between time of day, volume remaining or days to regeneration,
and tank in service (twin tank systems only).
•	 The Flow Indicator flashes when outlet flow is detected.

CARE AND USE OF YOUR BRINE TANK
Each time the softener regenerates, salty water (brine) is needed to recondition the media in the water tank.
The brine is pulled from the salt tank at a controlled amount. If the salt tank does not contain enough salt, the
brine is weak, the media will not fully recondition and untreated water will pass through. To ensure the highest
level of performance of your water conditioning system, please observe the following:
•	 Keep the brine tank filled with salt at all times. The salt level should always be higher than the water level
in the brine tank.
•	 Only use sodium chloride salt designed for water softeners. Other types of salt (rock or snow melting)
may contain dirt and chemicals that will affect the quality of your water and the performance of your
water softener.
•	 Keep the brine tank covered.
•	 Empty and clean the tank every three years.

raw_model_output:
The setup and calibration procedures for the Siemens MAG 6000 are as follows:

Setup Steps:
1. Mechanical Installation: Install the MAG 6000 transmitter as per the mechanical installation instructions. For the compact version, remove the terminal box lid, ensure the SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed, fit cable glands, unplug and connect coil and electrode cables, connect earth wire, and connect supply and output cables as per the electrical connection guidelines. The system will not register flow if black plugs are not connected to the connection board [Document 8, p.24].

2. Mounting: For remote mounting, ensure the power supply PE wire is connected to the PE terminal and the coil cable shield is connected to the SHIELD terminal. Mount the transmitter on the terminal box and tighten cable glands for optimum sealing. Avoid exposing the transmitter to direct sunlight to prevent increased operating temperature and decreased display visibility. A sun shield accessory is available [Document 4, p.30].

3. Commissioning: Commission the device via the local user interface (LUI). The display and menu functions allow changing passwords, basic settings, operator menu setup, and language. For MAG 5000/6000 Blind (without display), factory settings are uploaded from the SENSORPROM® unit after power-up. To change settings, replace the Blind transmitter with a standard transmitter, adjust settings via display and keypad, then remount the Blind transmitter. New settings are stored in the SENSORPROM® memory unit [Document 6, p.41].

Calibration Procedures:
1. Calibration Certificate: Each sensor is shipped with a calibration certificate and calibration data stored in the SENSORPROM memory unit. Reference conditions for calibration include medium temperature of 20°C ± 5°C, ambient temperature of 20°C ± 5°C, supply voltage within ±1%, and a warming-up time of 30 minutes. Proper flow conditions and pipe section lengths are also specified for accurate calibration [Document 3, p.69].

2. Recalibration: Siemens offers recalibration services for the sensor. The standard calibration offered is the standard matched pair calibration. For recalibration, the SENSORPROM® memory unit must always be returned with the sensor. Additional forms such as Delivery Note, Cover Note for Return Delivery, and Declaration of Decontamination must be provided when returning the device for recalibration. The device must be properly cleaned and free from hazardous residues before return [Document 1, p.62].

3. For custody transfer-approved MAG 5000/6000 CT transmitters, a hardware key is installed to lock software functions and seal the device to prevent changes. Calibration sealing is carried out at calibration [Document 4, p.30].

These steps ensure proper setup and accurate calibration of the Siemens MAG 6000 flowmeter.
returned_answer:
The setup and calibration procedures for the Siemens MAG 6000 are as follows:

Setup Steps:
1. Mechanical Installation: Install the MAG 6000 transmitter as per the mechanical installation instructions. For the compact version, remove the terminal box lid, ensure the SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed, fit cable glands, unplug and connect coil and electrode cables, connect earth wire, and connect supply and output cables as per the electrical connection guidelines. The system will not register flow if black plugs are not connected to the connection board [Document 8, p.24].

2. Mounting: For remote mounting, ensure the power supply PE wire is connected to the PE terminal and the coil cable shield is connected to the SHIELD terminal. Mount the transmitter on the terminal box and tighten cable glands for optimum sealing. Avoid exposing the transmitter to direct sunlight to prevent increased operating temperature and decreased display visibility. A sun shield accessory is available [Document 4, p.30].

3. Commissioning: Commission the device via the local user interface (LUI). The display and menu functions allow changing passwords, basic settings, operator menu setup, and language. For MAG 5000/6000 Blind (without display), factory settings are uploaded from the SENSORPROM® unit after power-up. To change settings, replace the Blind transmitter with a standard transmitter, adjust settings via display and keypad, then remount the Blind transmitter. New settings are stored in the SENSORPROM® memory unit [Document 6, p.41].

Calibration Procedures:
1. Calibration Certificate: Each sensor is shipped with a calibration certificate and calibration data stored in the SENSORPROM memory unit. Reference conditions for calibration include medium temperature of 20°C ± 5°C, ambient temperature of 20°C ± 5°C, supply voltage within ±1%, and a warming-up time of 30 minutes. Proper flow conditions and pipe section lengths are also specified for accurate calibration [Document 3, p.69].

2. Recalibration: Siemens offers recalibration services for the sensor. The standard calibration offered is the standard matched pair calibration. For recalibration, the SENSORPROM® memory unit must always be returned with the sensor. Additional forms such as Delivery Note, Cover Note for Return Delivery, and Declaration of Decontamination must be provided when returning the device for recalibration. The device must be properly cleaned and free from hazardous residues before return [Document 1, p.62].

3. For custody transfer-approved MAG 5000/6000 CT transmitters, a hardware key is installed to lock software functions and seal the device to prevent changes. Calibration sealing is carried out at calibration [Document 4, p.30].

These steps ensure proper setup and accurate calibration of the Siemens MAG 6000 flowmeter.

18 • F LECK 5800/5810/5812 XTRi Service Manual 
PENTAIR PRO: APP SETUP 
Pairing the Fleck  5800/5810/5812 XTRi Con­nected 
Valve with Wi-Fi Devices 
The Fleck  5800/5810/5812 XTRi Connected Valve can be paired 
with a smartphone or tablet. New users can download and install 
the Pentair Home App from the App Store or Google Play. WiFi 
connection must be 2.4 GHz.
Sign Up and Log In 
New users will need to create an account to monitor their water 
softeners. From the Log In page, press SIGN UP to create a new 
account. If you already have an account, skip to Login.
 Add your email address and set your password.
Once you select Create Account, an email will be sent to your 
email for verification.
 Click the “Verify Email” link to complete the process.

8 • FLECK 7000SXT Service Manual
MASTER PROGRAMMING MODE
When the Master Programming Mode is entered, all available
option setting displays may be viewed and set as needed.
Depending on current option settings, some parameters
cannot be viewed or set.
Setting the Time of Day
1.	 Press and hold either the Up or Down buttons until the
programming icon replaces the service icon and the
parameter display reads TD.
2.	 Adjust the displayed time with the Up and Down buttons.
3.	 When the desired time is set, press the Extra Cycle button
to resume normal operation. The unit will also return to
normal operation after 5 seconds if no buttons are pressed.
Entering Master Programming Mode
Set the Time Of Day display to 12:01 P.M. Press the Extra Cycle
button (to exit Setting Time of Day mode). Then press and hold
the Up and Down buttons together until the programming
icon replaces the service icon and the Display Format screen
appears.
Exiting Master Programming Mode
Press the Extra Cycle button to accept the displayed settings
and cycle to the next parameter. Press the Extra Cycle button
at the last parameter to save all settings and return to normal
operation. The control will automatically disregard any
programming changes and return to normal operation if it is
left in Master Programming mode for 5 minutes without any
keypad input.
Resets
Soft Reset: Press and hold the Extra Cycle and Down buttons
for 25 seconds while in normal Service mode.  This resets all

INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

[pentair_fleck_5800_5810_5812_manual_fleck_5800_5810_5812_xtri_manual.pdf|p=18|s=Page 18]
18 • F LECK 5800/5810/5812 XTRi Service Manual 
PENTAIR PRO: APP SETUP 
Pairing the Fleck  5800/5810/5812 XTRi Con­nected 
Valve with Wi-Fi Devices 
The Fleck  5800/5810/5812 XTRi Connected Valve can be paired 
with a smartphone or tablet. New users can download and install 
the Pentair Home App from the App Store or Google Play. WiFi 
connection must be 2.4 GHz.
Sign Up and Log In 
New users will need to create an account to monitor their water 
softeners. From the Log In page, press SIGN UP to create a new 
account. If you already have an account, skip to Login.
 Add your email address and set your password.
Once you select Create Account, an email will be sent to your 
email for verification.
 Click the “Verify Email” link to complete the process.

[pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4]
4 • FLECK 7000SXT Service Manual
INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

36 • FLECK
® 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual
GENERAL SERVICE HINTS FOR METER 
CONTROL
Problem: Softener delivers hard water
Reason: Reserve capacity has been exceeded. 
Correction: Check salt dosage requirements and reset 
program wheel to provide additional reserve.
Reason: Program wheel is not rotating with meter output.
Correction: Pull cable out of meter cover and rotate manually. 
Program wheel must move without binding and clutch must 
give positive clicks when program wheel strikes regeneration 
stop. If it does not, replace timer.
Reason: Meter is not measuring flow.
Correction: Check meter with meter checker.

Install MAG 5000 / MAG 6000 compact version 
1. Remove and discard terminal box lid of sensor. 
 
2. Ensure SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed. 
3. Fit M20 or ½" NPT cable glands for supply and output cables. 
4. Unplug the two black plug assemblies for coil and electrode cables in terminal box. 
5. Connect earth wire from connection board to bottom of terminal box. 
6. Connect 2-pin connector and 3-pin connector as shown to their corresponding terminal 
numbers on connection board as shown in Electrical connection (Page 36). 
 
Note 
System will not register flow if black plugs are not connected to connection board. 
 
7. Fit supply and output cables through cable glands and connect to connection plate as 
shown in Electrical connection (Page 36).

How do I troubleshoot Siemens MAG 5000?

raw_model_output:
To troubleshoot the Siemens MAG 5000, follow these steps based on the symptoms and error codes:

1. If the display is empty and output signals are minimum:
   - Check if there is power supply to the MAG 5000/6000.
   - Inspect the connector for bent pins.
   - If defective, replace the MAG 5000/6000.

2. If there is no flow signal and output signals are minimum:
   - Ensure current output and digital output are enabled.
   - Check for reverse flow direction and correct it.
   - For error code F70, check cables and connections for coil current issues.
   - For error code W31, ensure the measuring pipe is full.
   - For error code F60, replace the MAG 5000/6000 due to internal error.
   - For error code P42, check cables/connections or replace the device.
   - For error code P41, switch off the device for 5 seconds and switch on again.

3. If the device indicates flow with no flow in the pipe:
   - Select empty pipe cut-off or ensure the measuring pipe is full.
   - Check electrode connection and ensure the electrode cable is sufficiently screened.

4. For unstable flow signals:
   - Increase the time constant if there is pulsating flow or high concentration of particles.
   - Use special electrode cable if conductivity is too low.
   - Ensure sufficient potential equalization to avoid electrical noise.
   - Remove air bubbles from the medium.

5. For measuring errors:
   - Check installation correctness.
   - For error code P40, install SENSORPROM® unit.
   - For error code P44, replace or reset SENSORPROM® unit.

6. For other error codes:
   - F63: Replace defective SENSORPROM® unit.
   - F71: Replace MAG 5000/6000 due to loss of internal data.
   - W30: Check Qmax settings if flow exceeds 100%.
   - W21: Adjust volume/pulse or pulse width for pulse overflow.
   - W20: Reset totalizer manually for initializing error.
   - Missing electrode connection: Check cables.

7. If the display is defective, replace the display.
8. If the transmitter is defective, replace the transmitter.
9. If no replacement transmitter is available, check the transmitter according to the check table provided in the manual.

For further technical support, contact Siemens via their support request website or phone number provided in the manual.

These steps provide a comprehensive approach to troubleshooting the Siemens MAG 5000/6000 flowmeter system. 3. To cover several needs with just one pump size.

This allows you to use a DME for dosing a very small
quantity of liquid without having to change the input
signal.
Example:
A DME 375 receives a 12 mA input signal from a
control instrument. According to the analog curve (see
page 11), this results in a 50 % output and a capacity
of 188 l/h.
A new situation occurs where it is only necessary to
dose 47 l/h: The maximum capacity limitation is set to
94 l/h. The pump is still receiving a 12 mA signal
resulting in a 50 % output and a capacity of 47 l/h.

pump speed in timer-based batch control, pulse-based
batch control and during calibration where the pump
usually operates at maximum capacity.

8. Operation
8.1 Description of the pump
Fig. 13 DMX 227
Functional principle
•
Oscillating positive displacement pump with electric drive,
mechanical diaphragm deflection, and constant stroke length.
•
Following reduction of the motor speed by a worm gear, the
rotation of the drive is converted into the suction and
compression movement of the diaphragm by means of an
eccentric and tappet. A defined volume (stroke volume) of the
dosed medium is thus sucked into the dosing head via the
suction valve, and displaced into the dosing line by the
discharge valve.
•
The dosing flow can be adjusted in the range 1:10 if a
frequency converter is installed.
8.2 Switching on/off
•
To start the pump, switch on the power supply.
•
To stop the pump, switch off the power supply.
8.3 Adjustment of dosing flow using a frequency
converter
The dosing rate can only be adjusted in the range 1:10 if a
frequency converter is installed. See installation and operating
instructions for the frequency converter!
Settings of frequency converter when used with Grundfos
dosing pumps
Pay special attention to the following parameters of the frequency
converter:
•
P013 (maximum motor frequency):
– Set the frequency converter to maximum 100 Hz.
– Due to this setting, the maximum stroke frequency of the
pump cannot be exceeded.
•
P086 (motor current limit):
– Do not change the default setting (150 %).
– The motor is protected by a PTC resistor. Therefore, this
parameter is not necessary.

8. Operation
8.1 Description of the pump
Fig. 13 DMX 227
Functional principle
•
Oscillating positive displacement pump with electric drive,
mechanical diaphragm deflection, and constant stroke length.
•
Following reduction of the motor speed by a worm gear, the
rotation of the drive is converted into the suction and
compression movement of the diaphragm by means of an
eccentric and tappet. A defined volume (stroke volume) of the
dosed medium is thus sucked into the dosing head via the
suction valve, and displaced into the dosing line by the
discharge valve.
•
The dosing flow can be adjusted in the range 1:10 if a
frequency converter is installed.
8.2 Switching on/off
•
To start the pump, switch on the power supply.
•
To stop the pump, switch off the power supply.
8.3 Adjustment of dosing flow using a frequency
converter
The dosing rate can only be adjusted in the range 1:10 if a
frequency converter is installed. See installation and operating
instructions for the frequency converter!
Settings of frequency converter when used with Grundfos
dosing pumps
Pay special attention to the following parameters of the frequency
converter:
•
P013 (maximum motor frequency):
– Set the frequency converter to maximum 100 Hz.
– Due to this setting, the maximum stroke frequency of the
pump cannot be exceeded.
•
P086 (motor current limit):
– Do not change the default setting (150 %).
– The motor is protected by a PTC resistor. Therefore, this
parameter is not necessary.

START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

INSTALLATION & START-UP
Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
CAUTION  	Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to
freezing conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit.
NOTE:  	Be sure the tank is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve
to room temperature before operating.
3.	 Perform all plumbing according to local plumbing codes.
•	Use a 1/2-inch minimum pipe size for the drain.
•	Use a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates that
exceed 7 gpm or length that exceeds 20 feet (6 m).

3.6
Intended use
Circulating pump for domestic hot water systems.
If hot water is not used for longer periods of time, the water in the hot water pipe cools off.
Domestic hot water pumps (also called sanitary or drinking water circulating pumps) pump this
cold water back into the water heater via a separate recirculation pipe, or directly into the cold
water supply line (see Figure 5 and Figure 6 on page 19 and 20). At the same time fresh hot
water is flowing out of the water heater and provides a constant supply of hot water at the tap.
WARNING: Risk of electric shock
This pump has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas.
Do not install within an outer enclosure or beneath the skirt of a hot tub or spa.
This pump is not submersible.
CAUTION:
Acceptable for indoor use only. This pump has been evaluated for use with water only. Use with
maximum 203 °F (95 °C) water.
Pump selection
The e3-4 series models are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences with
a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m).
The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and
small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m).

Bell & Gossett e3-6 is making noise, what could be wrong?

raw_model_output:
If the Bell & Gossett e3-6 pump is making noise, several causes could be responsible:

- A check valve might be installed on the inlet side of the pump or installed in the wrong direction. The remedy is to check and correct the installation.
- The inlet side shut-off valve could be closed or clogged. The solution is to check and open or clean the valve.
- The system might not be thoroughly air purged. Refer to the air purge instructions or manually vent the system by opening the hose bib. For Autocirc pumps, turn off the pump and open hot and cold faucets to purge air.
- Foreign objects could be inside the pump. Disassemble the pump to remove any foreign objects.
- Worn bearings might cause the rotor to wobble during operation, requiring pump replacement.
- If the return line connects to the cold water supply at the top of the water heater, warm water may create back pressure in the cold supply line. Adding a check valve on the cold supply line above the return line tee connector can help.
- Noise occurring when an Autocirc pump turns off may be due to "water hammer."

These troubleshooting steps are detailed in the Bell & Gossett e3-4/e3-6 manual on page 39. [xylem_bell_gossett_e3_4_e3_6_iom_series_e3_4_e3_6_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=39|s=Page 39]

- The inlet side shut-off valve could be closed or clogged. The solution is to check and open or clean the valve.
- The system might not be thoroughly air purged. Refer to the air purge instructions or manually vent the system by opening the hose bib. For Autocirc pumps, turn off the pump and open hot and cold faucets to purge air.
- Foreign objects could be inside the pump. Disassemble the pump to remove any foreign objects.
- Worn bearings might cause the rotor to wobble during operation, requiring pump replacement.
- If the return line connects to the cold water supply at the top of the water heater, warm water may create back pressure in the cold supply line. Adding a check valve on the cold supply line above the return line tee connector can help.
- Noise occurring when an Autocirc pump turns off may be due to "water hammer."

These troubleshooting steps are detailed in the Bell & Gossett e3-4/e3-6 manual on page 39. [xylem_bell_gossett_e3_4_e3_6_iom_series_e3_4_e3_6_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=39|s=Page 39]

[xylem_bell_gossett_e3_4_e3_6_iom_series_e3_4_e3_6_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=14|s=Page 14]
of residences with a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m). The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m). Because the system is pressurized, the number of floors in a home is not taken into consideration
in sizing the circulating pump. The pump has only to produce continuous flow at a pressure
sufficient to overcome the friction losses created by the piping in the house water supply line
and the return line.
NOTICE: Water pressure
A recirculating system is a pressurized system operating at the city water pressure, as
determined by the pressure regulator on your line, or by a well pump, if you are on a well system.
In most residential plumbing systems, water pressure is set at 35 psi (241 kPa) and above.
Below 35 psi (241 kPa), water pressure may not be sufficient to fill the pipe diameter, leaving
space for air to accumulate in the lines.
If your system pressure is less than 35 psi (241 kPa), use the next larger pump on the Pump
Selection Guide.
NOTICE: Oversized pumps
Pumps should not be so large as to produce flow rates that may eventually erode holes in the
pipes. According to the Copper Development Association, excessive erosion occurs at a velocity
of about 5 ft (1.5 m) per second and higher; or about 4 gpm (15 l/min) in 1/2" Type M copper
pipe.
Use the recommended recirculation line size shown in the Pump Selection Guide. The e3 series
pumps are sized so that flow velocities are below these limits.

A recirculating system is a pressurized system operating at the city water pressure, as
determined by the pressure regulator on your line, or by a well pump, if you are on a well system.

Below 35 psi (241 kPa), water pressure may not be sufficient to fill the pipe diameter, leaving
space for air to accumulate in the lines.
If your system pressure is less than 35 psi (241 kPa), use the next larger pump on the Pump
Selection Guide.
NOTICE: Oversized pumps
Pumps should not be so large as to produce flow rates that may eventually erode holes in the
pipes. According to the Copper Development Association, excessive erosion occurs at a velocity
of about 5 ft (1.5 m) per second and higher; or about 4 gpm (15 l/min) in 1/2" Type M copper
pipe.

pumps are sized so that flow velocities are below these limits.

query: What are the safety requirements for installing Fleck 7000SXT?

[pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4]
4 • FLECK 7000SXT Service Manual
INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
CAUTION  	Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to
freezing conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit.
NOTE:  	Be sure the tank is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve
to room temperature before operating.
3.	 Perform all plumbing according to local plumbing codes.
•	Use a 1/2-inch minimum pipe size for the drain.
•	Use a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates that
exceed 7 gpm or length that exceeds 20 feet (6 m).

Press the Extra Cycle button. Use this display to set the

INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

raw_model_output:
To configure the Fleck 5800 XTR2, you can access various settings through the touchscreen control. Here are the key steps and features for configuration:

1. Turn on the screen by touching it.
2. You can enter the Assistance/Maintenance information such as the name and phone number of the water treatment professional or company that the homeowner may call for system service. This is optional and can be done using the keypad by pressing the buttons corresponding to the letters or numbers. After entering the information, press the accept button to save it.
3. Set the Assistance/Maintenance interval, which determines when the homeowner will need to call for service. This interval can be based on months or regenerations. Select the type of interval and then choose the number of months (up to 60) or regenerations (up to 2000). Press accept to save.
4. Adjust the Brightness/Sound settings to control the backlight of the control screen and mute alarms if needed. Note that these settings should only be accessed by a local water professional due to their complexity.
5. Use the Vacation Mode to halt all scheduled regenerations when needed; press again to resume normal operation.
6. Connect the control to a PC via USB for field programming or downloading diagnostic parameters using the Field Programmer application.
7. Navigate through screens using the screen navigation arrows and change values using the settings arrows. Remember to press accept to save changes or cancel to exit without saving.
8. Access Master Settings for all configurable parameters, but be cautious as improper adjustments may cause incorrect system operation. It is recommended to contact a professional water dealer before entering master settings.
9. The Assistance screen can be accessed from Master Settings or Home screens to view or change the service contact information.
10. If an alarm or error occurs, use the respective buttons to silence the alarm or view detailed error information.
11. Use the Advance arrow to move through cycle steps during regeneration.
12. Reset options are available in Diagnostics to reset Totalizer and Peak Flow data or in Master Settings to reset parameters to factory or non-factory settings.

Note: Settings cannot be accessed during a regeneration, and if a regeneration starts while in the settings menu, the screen will return to the main screen and all parameters will be voided.

These steps provide a comprehensive overview of configuring the Fleck 5800 XTR2 control system. For detailed instructions, refer to the specific sections in the service manual.

raw_model_output:
If a Fleck 9000 water conditioner is not responding, the following troubleshooting steps should be taken:

1. Check if electrical service to the unit has been interrupted. Assure permanent electrical service by checking the fuse, plug, pull chain, or switch.

2. Verify if the timer is defective. If so, replace the timer.

3. Confirm there has not been a power failure. If there was, reset the time of day.

4. Ensure the bypass valve is not open; if it is, close it.

5. Check if there is salt in the brine tank. Add salt and maintain the salt level above the water level if necessary.

6. Inspect the injector screen for plugging and clean it if needed.

7. Check that sufficient water is flowing into the brine tank by verifying the brine tank fill time and cleaning the brine line flow control if plugged.

8. Examine the distributor tube for leaks, cracks, or damaged O-ring and tube pilot.

9. Look for internal valve leaks and replace seals, spacers, and/or piston if required.

10. Review salt usage and salt setting to ensure the unit is not using too much salt or set improperly.

11. Investigate for excessive water in the brine tank.

12. Check for loss of water pressure.

13. Clean iron buildup in the line to the water conditioner and inside the water conditioner itself. Add mineral cleaner to the mineral bed and increase regeneration frequency if iron buildup is present.

14. Remove the piston and clean the control if the inlet of the control is plugged due to foreign material.

15. Assure that the well system has a proper air eliminator control and check for dry well condition to prevent loss of mineral through the drain line.

16. Verify that the drain line flow control is properly sized.

These steps are summarized from the problem and correction list for a water conditioner failing to regenerate in the Fleck 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual [pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=37|s=Page 37].

raw_model_output:
If the Fleck 9000 is not producing output, you should check the following:

1. Verify if the reserve capacity has been exceeded. If so, check salt dosage requirements and reset the program wheel to provide additional reserve.
2. Check if the program wheel is rotating with the meter output. Pull the cable out of the meter cover and rotate manually. The program wheel must move without binding and the clutch must give positive clicks when the program wheel strikes the regeneration stop. If it does not, replace the timer.
3. Confirm if the meter is measuring flow properly by checking the meter with a meter checker.

These steps are recommended to address the problem of the softener delivering hard water, which can be related to the meter not producing output [pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=36|s=Page 36].

Acceptance levels 
The following three acceptance levels are selectable. 
● Fatal error: Only fatal errors are registered as errors 
● Permanent error: Permanent and fatal errors are registered as errors 
● Warning (Default value): Warnings, permanent and fatal errors are registered as errors 
Error information is displayed in title and subtitle lines, see display layout (Page 40). Title line 
will show time since occurrence of error in days, hours and minutes. Subtitle line will flash 
between an error text and a remedy text. Error text will indicate type of error (I, W, P or F), 
error number, and error text. Remedy text will inform operator of action to take to remove 
error. 
 
Status log 
The latest 9 errors are stored in the status log. Errors are stored in the status log for 180 
days, even if they are corrected. 
Alarm field 
The alarm field on the display will always flash when an error is pending. 
Error output 
The digital and relay output can be activated individually error by error (error level). The relay 
output is default selected to error level. An output can also be selected to activate on a single 
error number. 
The alarm field, error output and error pending always operate together. 
Operator menu 
Error pending and status log are as default enabled (
) in the operator menu.

® 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual • 3
INSTALLATION & START-UP
Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
CAUTION  	Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to
freezing conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit.
NOTE:  	Be sure the tank is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve
to room temperature before operating.
3.	 Perform all plumbing according to local plumbing codes.
•	Use a 1/2-inch minimum pipe size for the drain.
•	Use a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates that
exceed 7 gpm or length that exceeds 20 feet (6 m).

for any reason prior to the delayed regeneration time, the
manual regeneration request shall be cleared. Pressing
the Extra Cycle button while in regeneration will cause the
upper drive to advance to the next step immediately.
Controller Operation During Regeneration
In the Regeneration Cycle step display, the controller shows the
current regeneration cycle name the valve is in, or has reached,
and the time remaining in that step. Once all regeneration steps
are complete, the controller returns to In Service and resumes
normal operation.
Press the Extra Cycle button during a system queued
Regeneration Cycle to immediately advance the valve
to the next cycle step position and resume normal
step timing.
Controller Operation During Programming
The controller enters the Program Mode in Standby or Service
Mode as long as it is not in regeneration. While in the Program
Mode, the controller continues to operate normally monitoring
water usage. Controller programming is stored in memory
permanently.
Controller Operation During A Power Failure
All program settings are stored in permanent memory. Current
valve position, cycle step time elapsed, and time of day are all
stored during a power failure, and will be restored when power

the main screen. 2. The control advances to Regeneration Cycle Step #1 (backwash), and begins programmed time count down. 3. the Extra Cycle button. To clear a queued
regeneration, press the Extra Cycle button again
to cancel. If regeneration occurs for any reason
prior to the delayed regeneration time, the manual
regeneration request will be cleared.
Control Operation During a Power Failure
The SXT includes integral power backup. In the event of power
failure, the control shifts into a power-saving mode. The control
stops monitoring water usage. The display and motor shut
down, but it continues to keep track of the time and day for a
minimum of 8 hours.
The system configuration settings are stored in a non-volatile
memory and are stored indefinitely with or without power.
The Time of Day flashes when there has been a power failure.
Press any button to stop the Time of Day from flashing.
If power fails while the unit is in regeneration, the control will
save the current valve position before it shuts down. When
power is restored, the control will resume the regeneration
cycle from the point where power failed.

go to step 4I. Press REGEN to return to previous step. STEP 4I – Next Regeneration Time (hour): Set the hour of day for regeneration using down or up arrow buttons. AM/PM toggles after 12. minutes of day regeneration using down or up arrow
buttons. This display not be shown if “on 0” is selected
in Step 9S or Step 7F. Press NEXT to exit Installer
Displays/ Settings. Press REGEN to return to previous
step.

and hold the “REGEN” button for three seconds.

control valve may be stepped through the various
regeneration cycles by pressing the “REGEN” button.
General Operation
User (U) Displays/Settings
When the system is operating one of two displays will be shown.
Pressing NEXT will alternate between the displays. One of the
displays is always the current time of day. The second display is one
of the following: days remaining or gallons remaining. Days remaining
are the number of days left before the system goes through a
regeneration cycle. Capacity remaining is the number of gallons that
will be treated before the system goes through a regeneration cycle.
The user can scroll between the displays as desired.
If the system has called for a regeneration that will occur at the preset
time of regeneration, the words REGEN TODAY will appear on the
display.
When water is being treated (i.e. water is flowing through the system)
the word “Softening” flashes on the display.

To configure the Siemens MAG 5000, you typically commission the device via the local user interface (LUI). The process involves using the display and keypad to change settings as needed. For the MAG 5000 Blind version, which does not have a display, all factory settings are uploaded from the SENSORPROM® unit after power-up. If other settings are required, you can use a standard transmitter with a display and similar power supply to change the settings. The changed data will be stored in the SENSORPROM® memory unit. Afterward, you remove the standard transmitter and remount the Blind transmitter, which will then upload the new settings stored in the SENSORPROM® memory unit. The detailed commissioning steps and menu functions are described in the Operating Instructions, including changing passwords, basic settings, operator menu setup, and language settings. For factory settings, refer to the Factory settings section in the manual.

1. Unscrew and remove MAG 5000/6000 Blind (if applicable).
2. Mount standard MAG 5000/6000 transmitter.
3. Change required settings via display and keypad.
4. All changed data will be stored in SENSORPROM® memory unit.
5. Remove standard transmitter and remount Blind transmitter.
6. Fasten screws holding transmitter.
7. New settings stored in SENSORPROM® memory unit will be uploaded in blind transmitter.

5.2 Checking the direction of rotation (three-phase motors) 
1. Place the unit in the vertical position on a level and flat surface.

5.3 Starting and stopping 
Float switch version 
1. Connect the plug to the mains and/or turn on the switch: depending on the position of the 
float, the unit stays idle or starts to operate.

• No liquid is leaking from the pipes 
• There is no unwanted noise or vibrations 
• There are no vortexes nearby the suction port 
• Liquid is actually being pumped. 
3. When the float reaches the low position (minimum liquid level), the pump automatically 
stops. 
Version without float switch 
1. Connect the plug to the mains and/or turn on the switch: the unit starts. 
2. With the unit in operation, complete the same checks as for the float version. 
3. Once the unit has taken up liquid to the minimum level, disconnect the plug from the mains 
and/or turn off the switch to switch it off.

The following three acceptance levels are selectable.

output is default selected to error level. An output can also be selected to activate on a single 
error number.

The commissioning process via the LUI includes changing settings such as password, basic settings, operator menu setup, and language. The device has a display and keypad for this purpose.
