MANUAL OVERVIEW
How To Use This Manual
This owner’s manual is designed to provide the homeowner with instructions on performing routine care and 
maintenance of the residential water softener or filter valve and control packaged with this manual.
This manual does not include instructions regarding installation, setup, service, or troubleshooting of the 
valve, control, or other components of a residential water conditioning system. Please contact your local 
water treatment professional with questions or concerns about the operation or performance of your water 
conditioning system.
Icons That Appear In This Manual
WARNING:  Failure to follow this instruction can result in personal injury or damage to the equipment.
NOTE: This will make the process easier if followed. 
General Warnings
WARNING:   There are no user-serviceable parts in the AC adapter, motor, or controller. Do not attempt to 
remove or repair individual components.
WARNING:   Use only the power transformer supplied with this water conditioning system.
WARNING:   The power outlet must be grounded and always on. If it is necessary to disconnect power, 
unplug the AC adapter from its power source.
WARNING:   Only fill the brine tank with salt designed for water softening.
WARNING:   Ambient temperature surrounding the system should be between 35°F (1°C) and 120°F 
(49°C).
WARNING:   Water temperature flowing through the system should be between 35°F (1°F) and 100°F 
(38°C).
California Proposition 65 Warning
WARNING:  This product contains chemicals known to the State of California to cause cancer or birth 
defects or other reproductive harm.
Pentair Fleck SXT Controller Service Manual • 3

GENERAL SERVICE HINTS FOR METER 
CONTROL
Problem: Softener delivers hard water
Reason: Reserve capacity has been exceeded. 
Correction: Check salt dosage requirements and reset 
program wheel to provide additional reserve.
Reason: Program wheel is not rotating with meter output.
Correction: Pull cable out of meter cover and rotate manually. 
Program wheel must move without binding and clutch must 
give positive clicks when program wheel strikes regeneration 
stop. If it does not, replace timer.
Reason: Meter is not measuring flow.
Correction: Check meter with meter checker.

INSTALLATION & START-UP
Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.

separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.

SETTING TIME OF DAY AND
INITIATING A MANUAL
REGENERATION
Setting the Time of Day
1.	 Press and hold either the Up or Down buttons until
the programming icon replaces the service icon and
the parameter display reads TD.
2.	 Adjust the displayed time with the Up and Down
buttons.
3.	 When the desired time is set, press the Extra Cycle
button to resume normal operation. The unit will
also return to normal operation after five seconds if
no buttons are pressed.
Queueing a Regeneration
1.	 Press the Extra Cycle button. The service icon will
flash to indicate that a regeneration is queued.
2.	 To cancel a queued regeneration, press the Extra
Cycle button.
Regenerating Immediately
Press and hold the Extra Cycle button for five seconds.
FEATURES OF THE PENTAIR FLECK SXT CONTROLLER
•	 Power backup that continues to keep time and the passage of days for a minimum of 8 hours in the event
of power failure. During a power outage, the control goes into a power-saving mode. It does not monitor
water usage during a power failure, but it does store the volume remaining at the time of power failure.
•	 Settings for both valve (basic system) and control type (method used to trigger a regeneration).
•	 Day-of-the-Week controls.
•	 While in service, the display alternates between time of day, volume remaining or days to regeneration,
and tank in service (twin tank systems only).
•	 The Flow Indicator flashes when outlet flow is detected.

How do I program Fleck SXT controller?

raw_model_output:
To program the Fleck SXT controller, follow these steps:

1. Enter User Programming Mode by pressing the Up and Down buttons simultaneously for five seconds while in service, ensuring the time of day is not set to 12:01 PM. This will allow you to adjust various settings such as Day Override (DO), Regeneration Time (RT), Feed Water Hardness (H), Fixed Reserve Capacity (RC), and Current Day of the Week (CD). Use the Extra Cycle button to move between these settings and the Up and Down buttons to adjust values. Press the Extra Cycle button to end User Programming Mode [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=11|s=Page 11][pentair_fleck_5810_5812sxt_manual_fleck_5810_5812_sxt_manual.pdf|p=6|s=Page 6].

2. To set the Time of Day, press and hold either the Up or Down buttons until the programming icon replaces the service icon and the parameter display reads TD. Adjust the displayed time with the Up and Down buttons. When the desired time is set, press the Extra Cycle button to resume normal operation. The unit will also return to normal operation after five seconds if no buttons are pressed [pentair_fleck_sxt_owners_manual_fleck_sxt_controllers_owner_s_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4][pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=8|s=Page 8].

3. For advanced settings, enter Master Programming Mode by setting the Time of Day display to 12:01 PM, pressing the Extra Cycle button to exit the Time of Day mode, then pressing and holding the Up and Down buttons together until the programming icon replaces the service icon and the Display Format screen appears. Use the Extra Cycle button to cycle through parameters and the Up and Down buttons to adjust settings. Press the Extra Cycle button at the last parameter to save all settings and return to normal operation. The control will automatically exit Master Programming Mode after five minutes of inactivity [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=8|s=Page 8].

4. Additional features include queueing a regeneration by pressing the Extra Cycle button, canceling a queued regeneration by pressing the Extra Cycle button again, and initiating an immediate regeneration by pressing and holding the Extra Cycle button for five seconds [pentair_fleck_sxt_owners_manual_fleck_sxt_controllers_owner_s_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4].

These steps provide a comprehensive approach to programming the Fleck SXT controller. For detailed parameter descriptions and additional settings, refer to the specific programming sections in the manuals.

Setting the Time of Day

Queueing a Regeneration

2.	 To cancel a queued regeneration, press the Extra
Cycle button.
Regenerating Immediately
Press and hold the Extra Cycle button for five seconds.
FEATURES OF THE PENTAIR FLECK SXT CONTROLLER
•	 Power backup that continues to keep time and the passage of days for a minimum of 8 hours in the event
of power failure. During a power outage, the control goes into a power-saving mode. It does not monitor
water usage during a power failure, but it does store the volume remaining at the time of power failure.
•	 Settings for both valve (basic system) and control type (method used to trigger a regeneration).
•	 Day-of-the-Week controls.
•	 While in service, the display alternates between time of day, volume remaining or days to regeneration,
and tank in service (twin tank systems only).
•	 The Flow Indicator flashes when outlet flow is detected.

operation. The control will automatically disregard any
programming changes and return to normal operation if it is
left in Master Programming mode for 5 minutes without any
keypad input.

INSTALLATION & START-UP
Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
CAUTION  	Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to
freezing conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit.
NOTE:  	Be sure the tank is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve
to room temperature before operating.
3.	 Perform all plumbing according to local plumbing codes.
•	Use a 1/2-inch minimum pipe size for the drain.
•	Use a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates that
exceed 7 gpm or length that exceeds 20 feet (6 m).

Fleck 9000 is not starting, what should I check?

raw_model_output:
If the Fleck 9000 is not starting, you should check the following:

1. Assure permanent electrical service by checking the fuse, plug, pull chain, or switch to ensure the unit has continuous power supply.
2. Verify that the timer is not defective; if it is, replace the timer.
3. Check for any power failure and reset the time of day if necessary.
4. Make sure the bypass valve is closed.
5. Confirm that the meter is measuring flow correctly by checking the meter with a meter checker.
6. Pull the cable out of the meter cover and rotate manually to ensure the program wheel is rotating with the meter output and moves without binding.
7. Verify that the program wheel clutch gives positive clicks when it strikes the regeneration stop; if it does not, replace the timer.

INSTALLATION & START-UP
Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
CAUTION  	Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to
freezing conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit.
NOTE:  	Be sure the tank is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve
to room temperature before operating.
3.	 Perform all plumbing according to local plumbing codes.
•	Use a 1/2-inch minimum pipe size for the drain.
•	Use a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates that
exceed 7 gpm or length that exceeds 20 feet (6 m).

START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

DOC submersible pump is not producing output, what should I check?

raw_model_output:
If your DOC submersible pump is not producing output, you should check the following:

1. Ensure the discharge valve is fully open.
2. Verify that the pump speed is correct and that the driver is receiving full voltage.
3. Confirm the pump rotation is correct (should be counterclockwise when viewed from above).
4. Inspect for any obstruction in the liquid passage, including the suction strainer, impeller, and bowls.
5. Check if the water level in the well is above the first stage impeller; if not, increase the pump setting by adding column.
6. Verify that the static lift is not too high by checking the dynamic water level in the well.
7. Ensure the field head requirement does not exceed the design head; if it does, consider increasing discharge piping size or adding stages/increasing impeller diameter.
8. Inspect for damaged bowl assembly or broken/disconnected shaft and repair as necessary.
9. Check if the driver has reduced voltage or current and ensure it reaches the proper speed.

These steps are summarized from the troubleshooting section for pumps not delivering liquid and related issues [xylem_goulds_water_technology_dwt_iom_deep_well_turbine_pumps_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=22|s=Page 22].

raw_model_output:
The setup steps for the Siemens MAG 5000 include changing basic settings as follows: After entering setup mode, you can change individual settings such as positioning the decimal point and setting units for flow rate in totalizer 1 and totalizer 2. To change other settings, repeat the steps of selecting the parameter and adjusting the value. Finally, press the top up key two times to exit setup mode [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=46|s=Page 46].

Regarding calibration procedures, Siemens offers recalibration services for the MAG 5000 sensor. The standard calibration offered is a standard matched pair calibration. For recalibration, the SENSORPROM® memory unit must always be returned with the sensor. Additionally, when returning the device for recalibration, a delivery note, a cover note with product and return information, and a declaration of decontamination certifying that the device is free from residues must be provided. If the device has been used with hazardous substances, it must be cleaned properly before return. Shipments without a declaration of decontamination will be cleaned professionally at the customer's expense before further processing [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=62|s=Page 62].

In summary, setup involves parameter adjustments in setup mode with exit by pressing the top up key twice, and calibration involves returning the sensor with SENSORPROM and proper documentation for Siemens to perform standard matched pair recalibration [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=46|s=Page 46][siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=62|s=Page 62].

Changing Length of Brine Tank Refill Time
The second group of holes on the program wheel determines
the length of time the water conditioner refills the brine tank
(2 minutes per hole).
To change the length of refill time, move the two pins at the
end of the second group of holes as required.
The Regeneration cycle is complete when the two pin set at
end of the brine tank refill section trips the outer
micro-switch. The program wheel, however, continues to
rotate until the inner micro-switch drops into the notch on the
program wheel.
Programming
1.	 The control valve is set at the factory for backwash; brine
and slow rinse; rapid rinse and brine tank fill times.
Change any of these times by repositioning the pins and
holes or adding more pins.
NOTE:  	Two timer motors are available.
1/15 RPM has 82 minute Regeneration Time and
each pin or hole equals one minute.
1/30 RPM has 164 minute Regeneration Time and
each pin or hole equals two minutes.
2.	 The control valve has a separate brine tank fill cycle.
Calculate the desired salt setting using the brine line
flow control rate of refill (in gpm) multiplied by the timer
setting. Then, using one gallon of fresh water dissolving
approximately 3 lbs salt, calculate the refill time.

raw_model_output:
The provided documents do not contain specific step-by-step instructions for performing maintenance on the Fleck 9000 water conditioner. However, some general troubleshooting and service hints are available:

- If the water conditioner fails to regenerate, check for electrical service interruptions, timer defects, power failures, open bypass valve, salt level in the brine tank, plugged injector screen, insufficient water flow into the brine tank, leaks, internal valve leaks, improper salt settings, excessive water in the brine tank, loss of water pressure, iron buildup, and air in the water system. Correct these issues accordingly, such as replacing the timer, adding salt, cleaning screens, closing valves, replacing seals, and cleaning lines or controls as needed [Document 1, p.37].

- For meter control issues, if the softener delivers hard water, check salt dosage requirements and reset the program wheel to provide additional reserve. If the program wheel is not rotating with meter output, manually rotate the program wheel and check for binding or clutch issues; replace the timer if necessary. Also, check the meter with a meter checker if it is not measuring flow [Document 4, p.36].

- When servicing the control valve, cycle the timer through backwash, brine, slow rinse, rapid rinse, and brine tank refill positions, waiting for the control drive motor to position itself and stop before advancing to the next position. This helps backwash air from the tanks and ensures proper valve positioning [Document 2, p.4].

- Adjust the length of brine tank refill time by moving pins on the program wheel as needed, based on the brine line flow control rate and desired salt setting [Document 3, p.5].

For detailed maintenance procedures, consult the full Fleck 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual or contact a water treatment professional [Documents 1, 2, 3, 4].

raw_model_output:
The installation of a DOC submersible pump involves several steps and precautions:

1. Ensure the installation site is suitable, with a non-aggressive, non-explosive atmosphere, and not subjected to frost. The temperature of the pumped liquid should be between 0 to 40°C (32 to 104°F) [Document 7].

2. Check the inside diameter of the well and the maximum outside diameter of the pump assembly to ensure adequate clearance for installation. The well must be straight to avoid binding and distortion of the pump column. If the straightness is unknown, gauge the well with a dummy assembly slightly larger than the pump bowl assembly [Document 6].

3. Develop the well with a test pump to remove excess sand and determine capacity and drawdown. The well capacity should equal or exceed the pump capacity to avoid cavitation or damage [Document 6].

4. The pump must be equipped with enough column pipe to keep the bowl assembly submerged during operation [Document 6].

5. Before electrical connections, ensure the unit is unplugged and cannot restart unintentionally. Always connect the external protection conductor (ground) to the ground terminal first [Document 5].

6. For electrical connection, a qualified technician should complete all hydraulic and electrical connections according to current regulations [Document 5].

7. When installing the pump, loosen the screw ring, rotate the pump motor to the required installation position, and then tighten the screw ring. For horizontal installation, the timer should point upwards and may be turned within a ±45° range to maintain ingress protection [Document 4].

8. Insert the cable through the threaded hole into the motor housing, connect each stripped core into the proper terminal block hole, ensuring correct color matching and that the entire stripped conductor length is inside the terminal block. Insert the cable gland components and tighten the nut. Reassemble the end cap in the correct orientation and tighten the screw [Document 8].

9. Before energizing the electrical connection, fill the pump unit with water to prevent bearing damage from dry operation [Document 8].

10. Place the unit in the vertical position on a level and flat surface. For three-phase motors, check the direction of rotation by starting and stopping the unit immediately; the impulse movement should be clockwise [Document 3].

11. Connect the plug to the mains and/or turn on the switch. For float switch versions, the unit will start or stay idle depending on the float position. Check for leaks, noise, vibrations, vortexes near the suction port, and confirm liquid is being pumped. The pump will stop automatically when the float reaches the low position [Document 3].

12. Ensure the suction port is completely submerged in the liquid before start-up [Document 7].

These steps summarize the installation process and precautions for the DOC submersible pump. For detailed diagrams and specific technical data, refer to the full installation manual [Documents 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8].

- Verify that the day override is set properly.
- Ensure the meter cable is connected properly.
- Confirm that the meter is functioning properly.

- Check that the correct system capacity and meter size have been selected.
- Also, watch for the flow indicator on the display to confirm flow measurement.

INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

For a Lowara DOC pump that is not responding, the troubleshooting steps are as follows:

1. Check if the power supply is cut off and restore it if necessary.
2. Adjust the float if it is low.
3. Replace blown fuses.
4. Reset the thermal overload protection on the control panel, check the liquid level, or disconnect the electric power supply and wait 2 minutes before reconnecting it if the thermal overload protection of the motor has been triggered.
5. Contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor for replacement if the supply cord is damaged.
6. Check and repair or replace the control panel if it is faulty.

How do I configure Fleck 5800 XTR2?

raw_model_output:
To configure the Fleck 5800 XTR2, you will primarily interact with the touchscreen control and its settings menus. Here are the key steps and features involved in configuration:

1. Turning on the Screen: Touch the screen to activate it.

2. Assistance/Maintenance Information: You can enter the name and phone number of the water treatment professional or company that the homeowner may call for system service. This is optional and can be done using the keypad on the screen. You can also set an assistance interval, which determines when the homeowner will need to call for service, based on months or regenerations. This is done through the Assistance/Mainten. Interval screen.

3. Brightness/Sound Settings: Adjust the backlight of the control screen and mute alarms if needed. Note that these settings should be accessed by a local water professional due to their complexity.

4. Master Settings: These include all configurable parameters available in the control. Accessing Master Settings requires caution as improper adjustments may cause the system to operate incorrectly. A warning message appears before entering Master Settings, and a password is required.

5. Other Features: Vacation Mode can be enabled to halt all scheduled regenerations temporarily. USB Connect allows connection to a PC for field programming or downloading diagnostic parameters.

6. Navigation and Saving Changes: Use screen navigation arrows to move between screens. Use settings arrows to change values. Press the Accept button to save changes or Cancel to exit without saving.

7. Alarms and Errors: When an alarm or error occurs, the screen will display relevant information, and you can silence alarms or view detailed error information.

It is recommended to contact a professional water dealer before entering Master Settings to avoid incorrect system operation.

These instructions provide an overview of the configuration process for the Fleck 5800 XTR2 control system. For detailed steps and illustrations, refer to the specific pages in the service manual.

raw_model_output:
To troubleshoot the Siemens MAG 5000, follow these steps based on the symptoms and error codes:

1. If the display is empty and the output signals are minimum:
   - Check for power supply issues.
   - Inspect the MAG 5000/6000 for bent pins on the connector.
   - If defective, replace the MAG 5000/6000.

2. If there is no flow signal and output signals are minimum:
   - Ensure the current output is enabled.
   - Ensure the digital output is enabled.
   - Check for reverse flow direction and correct it.
   - Error codes such as F70 indicate incorrect or no coil current; check cables and connections.
   - W31 indicates the measuring pipe is empty; ensure it is full.
   - F60 indicates an internal error; replace the MAG 5000/6000.

3. For undefined errors like P42:
   - Check for no load on current output and verify cables/connections.
   - Replace MAG 5000/6000 if defective.

4. For initializing errors (P41):
   - Switch off the MAG 5000/6000, wait 5 seconds, and switch it on again.

5. If the device indicates flow with no flow in the pipe:
   - Select empty pipe cut-off.
   - Ensure the measuring pipe is full.
   - Check electrode connection and ensure the electrode cable is sufficiently screened.

6. For unstable flow signals:
   - Increase the time constant if pulsating flow is present.
   - Use a special electrode cable if the conductivity of the medium is too low.
   - Ensure sufficient potential equalization to avoid electrical noise.
   - Remove air bubbles from the medium.
   - Increase the time constant if there is a high concentration of particles or fibers.

7. For measuring errors:
   - Check installation correctness.
   - Install or replace SENSORPROM® unit if indicated by error codes P40 or F63.
   - Reset or replace SENSORPROM® unit if indicated by P44.

8. For maximum output signals:
   - Check if flow exceeds 100% of Qmax (W30).
   - Adjust volume/pulse or pulse width if pulse overflow occurs (W21).

9. For loss of totalizer data or initializing errors (W20):
   - Reset the totalizer manually.

10. If the display shows error triangles or incorrect readings:
    - Refer to the error table for specific error codes.
    - Replace the display if defective.
    - Replace the transmitter if defective.

For detailed checks, Siemens recommends replacing the transmitter with a similar MAG 5000/6000 to verify if the issue is with the transmitter or sensor. All settings are stored in the SENSORPROM®, so replacement is straightforward without extra settings. If no replacement transmitter is available, follow the transmitter check table starting with powering on the transmitter and checking the display light and error triangles.

For further technical support, contact Siemens via their internet support request or phone number provided in the documentation.

These steps provide a comprehensive approach to troubleshooting the Siemens MAG 5000 flowmeter. [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=63|p=64|p=59|p=60]

How do I troubleshoot DOC submersible pump?

raw_model_output:
To troubleshoot a DOC submersible pump, follow these steps based on common issues and their remedies:

1. The unit does not start:
- Check if the power supply is cut off and restore it if necessary.
- Adjust the float if it is in the low position.
- Replace blown fuses.
- Reset the thermal overload protection on the control panel, check the liquid level, or disconnect and reconnect the power supply after 2 minutes.
- Contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor if the supply cord is damaged.
- Check and repair or replace the control panel if faulty. [Document 4, p.21]

2. The unit runs but there is little or no flow rate:
- Increase the installation depth or adjust the float if the tank liquid level is too low.
- Remove any foreign bodies in the unit.
- Remove any throttling in the discharge pipe.
- Remove clogging in piping and/or unit.
- Contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor if the unit is undersized. [Document 8, p.22]

3. The unit never stops:
- Check and correct the motor rotation direction.
- Adjust the float correctly.
- Release the float if it cannot move freely.
- Contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor if the float is faulty.
- Contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor if the unit is undersized.
- Contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor if the impeller is worn. [Document 8, p.22]

4. Thermal overload protection triggers:
- Contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor if the liquid temperature is high.
- Remove solid or fibrous substances causing unit overload.
- Recalibrate if the protection is set too low relative to the motor's rated current.
- Ensure input voltage is within rated limits and balanced across phases.
- Adjust flow rate to be within permitted limits.
- Check if the impeller is seized. [Document 4, p.21]

If faults cannot be corrected or are not mentioned, contact Xylem or the Authorized Distributor for assistance. [Document 4, p.21]

The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m). Because the system is pressurized, the number of floors in a home is not taken into consideration
in sizing the circulating pump. The pump has only to produce continuous flow at a pressure
sufficient to overcome the friction losses created by the piping in the house water supply line
and the return line.
NOTICE: Water pressure
A recirculating system is a pressurized system operating at the city water pressure, as
determined by the pressure regulator on your line, or by a well pump, if you are on a well system.
In most residential plumbing systems, water pressure is set at 35 psi (241 kPa) and above.
Below 35 psi (241 kPa), water pressure may not be sufficient to fill the pipe diameter, leaving
space for air to accumulate in the lines.
If your system pressure is less than 35 psi (241 kPa), use the next larger pump on the Pump
Selection Guide.
NOTICE: Oversized pumps
Pumps should not be so large as to produce flow rates that may eventually erode holes in the
pipes. According to the Copper Development Association, excessive erosion occurs at a velocity
of about 5 ft (1.5 m) per second and higher; or about 4 gpm (15 l/min) in 1/2" Type M copper
pipe.
Use the recommended recirculation line size shown in the Pump Selection Guide. The e3 series
pumps are sized so that flow velocities are below these limits.

Figure 5  Program Wheel
19.	Cycle timer into backwash position. Turn manual knob so
that the micro switch rides on the first set of pins. In this
position the tanks switch (lower piston) and the control
valve moves to the backwash position (upper piston). Wait
until the positioning of upper and lower pistons stops
before advancing the timer further. If advanced too fast
the control will not home into the In Service position (it
will not advance to any other position). To correct this,
rotate the manual knob back to In Service and start again
into backwash.
NOTE:  	Once valve positions itself into the backwash cycle,
the homing circuit locks in.
20.	With all the air backwashed, slowly cycle the timer to the
brine position; rapid rinse; and brine tank refill. Wait for
the control drive motor to position itself in each cycle and
stop, before advancing on to the next position.
21.	Once back in the In Service position, cycle the control
valve again into the backwash position. The tanks switch
again, and air head backwashes out of the other tank.
Cycle the control back to the In Service position. Leave the
timer in the open position. DO NOT insert meter cable yet.
NOTE:  	Two motors are available.
1/15 RPM has 82 minute regeneration time.
1/30 RPM has 164 minute regeneration time.
Valve To Tank Installation
1.	 Spin the valve onto the tank, ensuring the threads are not
cross-threaded.

How do I perform maintenance on Fleck 9000?

raw_model_output:
The provided documents do not contain specific step-by-step instructions for performing maintenance on the Fleck 9000 water conditioner. However, some general troubleshooting and service hints are available:

- If the water conditioner fails to regenerate, check for electrical service interruptions, timer defects, power failures, open bypass valve, salt level in the brine tank, plugged injector screen, insufficient water flow into the brine tank, leaks, internal valve leaks, improper salt settings, excessive water in the brine tank, loss of water pressure, iron buildup, and air in the water system. Correct these issues as indicated (e.g., replace timer, add salt, clean screens, close bypass valve) [Document 1, p.37].

- For meter control issues such as softener delivering hard water, check salt dosage, ensure the program wheel rotates properly with the meter output, and verify the meter is measuring flow correctly. Replace the timer if the program wheel does not move properly [Document 4, p.36].

- To adjust the length of the brine tank refill time, move the pins on the program wheel as required. The refill time is determined by the second group of holes on the program wheel, with each hole representing 2 minutes of refill time. Calculate the desired salt setting based on the brine line flow control rate and timer setting [Document 3, p.5].

- For air removal, cycle the timer through backwash, brine, slow rinse, rapid rinse, and brine tank refill positions, waiting for the control drive motor to position itself in each cycle before advancing [Document 2, p.4].

These points provide some guidance on maintenance-related checks and adjustments but do not constitute a full maintenance procedure. For detailed maintenance instructions, refer to the full service manual or contact a water treatment professional [Documents 1, 2, 3, 4].

raw_model_output:
To configure the Fleck 5800 SXT, you need to set various option settings using the control interface. One of the key settings is the Regenerant Flow, identified by "RF" in the upper left corner of the screen. There are seven possible settings for this parameter, including Downflow/Upflow Single Backwash, Other Upflow, Other Downflow, Upflow Refill First, Upflow Brine First, Filter, and Downflow Double Backwash. Fleck 7000SXT is not producing output, what should I check?

raw_model_output:
If the Fleck 7000SXT water conditioner is not producing output, you should check the following potential causes and corrections:

- Electrical service to the unit may have been interrupted. Assure permanent electrical service by checking the fuse, plug, pull chain, or switch.
- The timer could be defective. Replace the timer if necessary.
- There might have been a power failure. Reset the time of day.
- The bypass valve could be open. Close the bypass valve.
- No salt in the brine tank. Add salt and maintain the salt level above the water level.
- Injector screen might be plugged. Clean the injector screen.
- Insufficient water flowing into the brine tank. Check the brine tank fill time and clean the brine line flow control if plugged.
- Leak at distributor tube. Make sure the distributor tube is not cracked and check the O-ring and tube pilot.
- Internal valve leak. Replace seals and spacers and/or piston.
- Improper salt setting or unit used too much salt. Check salt usage and salt setting.
- Excessive water in the brine tank.
- Loss of water pressure.
- Iron buildup in the line to the water conditioner or in the water conditioner itself. Clean the line and control and add mineral cleaner to the mineral bed. Increase frequency of regeneration.
- Inlet of control plugged due to foreign material. Remove piston and clean control.
- Loss of mineral through drain line.
- Air in water system. Assure that the well system has proper air eliminator control and check for dry well condition.
- Improperly sized drain line flow control.

These checks and corrections are detailed in the troubleshooting section of the Fleck 7000SXT Service Manual (page 17) [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=17|s=Page 17].

The refill flow control is a flexible washer-like part with a small orifice and a precision molded contour that delivers a steady 0.5 gpm regenerant tank refill rate at varying inlet pressures. assembly is attached to the control valve with a locking clip. The
locking clip allows the elbow to rotate 270 degrees so the outlet can
be orientated towards the regenerant tank.

and a fitting. The drain line flow control allows proper media bed
expansion by regulating the flow rate to the drain.

over the pressure range of 1-0 psi to 125 psi. The flexible washer-like

MAG 5000/6000 compact 
Install MAG 5000 / MAG 6000 compact version 
1. Remove and discard terminal box lid of sensor. 
 
2. Ensure SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed. 
3. Fit M20 or ½" NPT cable glands for supply and output cables. 
4. Unplug the two black plug assemblies for coil and electrode cables in terminal box. 
5. Connect earth wire from connection board to bottom of terminal box. 
6. Connect 2-pin connector and 3-pin connector as shown to their corresponding terminal 
numbers on connection board as shown in Electrical connection (Page 36).

7. Fit supply and output cables through cable glands and connect to connection plate as 
shown in Electrical connection (Page 36).
What are the installation requirements and error code meanings for Siemens MAG 6000?

raw_model_output:
The installation requirements for the Siemens MAG 6000 include the following key points: The MAG 6000 compact version installation involves removing and discarding the terminal box lid of the sensor, ensuring the SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed, fitting M20 or ½" NPT cable glands for supply and output cables, unplugging the two black plug assemblies for coil and electrode cables in the terminal box, connecting the earth wire from the connection board to the bottom of the terminal box, and connecting the 2-pin and 3-pin connectors to their corresponding terminal numbers on the connection board as shown in the electrical connection instructions. It is important to note that the system will not register flow if the black plugs are not connected to the connection board. Finally, supply and output cables should be fitted through cable glands and connected to the connection plate as per the electrical connection guidelines [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=24|s=Page 24].

Regarding error code meanings for the Siemens MAG 6000, several codes and their causes/remedies are documented:

- F70: Incorrect or no coil current; remedy is to check cables/connections.
- W31: Measuring pipe empty; ensure the measuring pipe is full.
- F60: Internal error; replace MAG 5000/6000.
- P42: No load on current output; check cables/connections or replace MAG 5000/6000.
- P41: Initializing error; switch off MAG 5000/6000, wait 5 seconds, and switch on again.
- Undefined error indicating flow with no flow in pipe; ensure the measuring pipe is full, select empty pipe cut-off, and ensure electrode cable is connected and sufficiently screened.
- F63: Defective SENSORPROM® unit; replace SENSORPROM® unit.
- F71: Loss of internal data; replace MAG 5000/6000.
- W30: Flow exceeds 100% of Qmax; check Qmax settings.
- W21: Pulse overflow; adjust volume/pulse or pulse width.
- P43: Internal error due to too many errors at the same time; switch off and on.
- P44: CT SENSORPROM® unit used incorrectly; replace or reset SENSORPROM® unit.
- F62: SENSORPROM® ID does not comply with product ID; replace SENSORPROM® unit.
- F63: SENSORPROM® unit unreadable; replace SENSORPROM® unit.
- F70: Coil excitation failure; check cables.
- F71: Internal conversion error in ASIC; replace transmitter.

The installation requirements for the Siemens MAG 6000 include the following key points: The MAG 6000 compact version installation involves removing and discarding the terminal box lid of the sensor, ensuring the SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed, fitting M20 or ½" NPT cable glands for supply and output cables, unplugging the two black plug assemblies for coil and electrode cables in the terminal box, connecting the earth wire from the connection board to the bottom of the terminal box, and connecting the 2-pin and 3-pin connectors to their corresponding terminal numbers on the connection board as shown in the electrical connection instructions. It is important to note that the system will not register flow if the black plugs are not connected to the connection board. Finally, supply and output cables should be fitted through cable glands and connected to the connection plate as per the electrical connection guidelines [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=24|s=Page 24].

Regarding error code meanings for the Siemens MAG 6000, several codes and their causes/remedies are documented:

- F70: Incorrect or no coil current; remedy is to check cables/connections.
- W31: Measuring pipe empty; ensure the measuring pipe is full.
- F60: Internal error; replace MAG 5000/6000.
- P42: No load on current output; check cables/connections or replace MAG 5000/6000.
- P41: Initializing error; switch off MAG 5000/6000, wait 5 seconds, and switch on again.
- Undefined error indicating flow with no flow in pipe; ensure the measuring pipe is full, select empty pipe cut-off, and ensure electrode cable is connected and sufficiently screened.
- F63: Defective SENSORPROM® unit; replace SENSORPROM® unit.
- F71: Loss of internal data; replace MAG 5000/6000.
- W30: Flow exceeds 100% of Qmax; check Qmax settings.
- W21: Pulse overflow; adjust volume/pulse or pulse width.
- P43: Internal error due to too many errors at the same time; switch off and on.
- P44: CT SENSORPROM® unit used incorrectly; replace or reset SENSORPROM® unit.
- F62: SENSORPROM® ID does not comply with product ID; replace SENSORPROM® unit.
- F63: SENSORPROM® unit unreadable; replace SENSORPROM® unit.
- F70: Coil excitation failure; check cables.
- F71: Internal conversion error in ASIC; replace transmitter.

What is the procedure for replacing impeller on Bell & Gossett e3-4?

raw_model_output:
The procedure for replacing the impeller on a Bell & Gossett e3-4 pump involves the following steps:

1. Check for any foreign objects in the rotor cavity and remove them if found.
2. Remove the rotor from the stator by grasping the impeller blades and gently pulling straight up. Avoid pulling up on one side only or pushing the rotor sideways.
3. Inspect the rotor cavity and magnet surface for wear marks. If there are many wear marks, the pump has worn off and the rotor should be replaced.
4. If no issues are found, reinstall the rotor into the stator carefully. Do not let the rotor drop onto the ceramic bearing; lower it slowly and then spin the rotor with your fingers to ensure it turns freely.
5. For reconnection or new pump installation, follow the installation rules.

This information is found in the Bell & Gossett e3-4 installation, operation, and maintenance manual on page 37.

query: What are the safety requirements for installing Fleck 9000?
final_context_preview:
[pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=3|s=Page 3]
FLECK
® 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual • 3
INSTALLATION & START-UP
Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
CAUTION  	Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to
freezing conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit.
NOTE:  	Be sure the tank is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve
to room temperature before operating.
3.	 Perform all plumbing according to local plumbing codes.
•	Use a 1/2-inch minimum pipe size for the drain.
•	Use a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates that
exceed 7 gpm or length that exceeds 20 feet (6 m).

What are the safety requirements for installing Fleck 9000?

raw_model_output:
The safety requirements for installing the Fleck 9000 include the following:

- Water pressure must be a minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) for the regeneration valve to operate effectively, and it must not exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar).
- Water temperature should not exceed 110°F (43°C).
- The unit must not be subjected to freezing conditions.
- The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air breaks and backflow.
- Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.
- The unit should be placed on a level and firm base.
- During cold weather, the valve should be warmed to room temperature before operating.
- Plumbing must be performed according to local plumbing codes.
- Use a minimum 1/2-inch pipe size for the drain, and a 3/4-inch drain line for backwash flow rates exceeding 7 gpm or lengths exceeding 20 feet (6 m).

These requirements ensure proper and safe operation of the Fleck 9000 water softener system. [pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=3|s=Page 3]

Water Pressure
A minimum of 25 pounds (1.7 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
A continuous 115 volt, 60 Hertz current supply is required.
Make certain the current supply is always hot and cannot be
turned off with another switch.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron,
a separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the
water softener.

The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
Bypass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve.

freezing conditions.

Error Codes and Troubleshooting
Detected Errors
If a communication error is detected, an Error Screen will appear.
• All units In Service remain in the In Service position.
• All units in Standby go to In Service.
• Any unit in Regeneration when the error occurs completes
Regeneration and goes to In Service.
• No units are allowed to start a Regeneration Cycle while the
error condition exists, unless they are manually forced into
Regeneration.
• When an error is corrected and the error no longer displays
(it may take several seconds for all of the units in a system to
stop displaying the error message), the system returns to
normal operation.
NOTE:  During the error condition, the control continues
to monitor the flow meter and update the volume remain-
ing. Once the error condition is corrected, all units return
to the operating status they were in prior to the error.
Regeneration queue is rebuilt according to the normal sys-
tem operation. Or, if more than one unit has been queued
for regeneration, then the queue is rebuilt according to
which one communicates first.

If a communication error is detected, an Error Screen will appear.

1. Check the integrity of the supply cord and replace it if damaged by contacting Xylem or the Authorized Distributor for replacement parts [xylem_lowara_doc_iom_doc_submersible_pump_units_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=20|s=Page 20].

2. Spare parts can be identified and ordered using product codes available on the website www.lowara.com/spark, and technical information can be obtained from Xylem or the Authorized Distributor [xylem_lowara_doc_iom_doc_submersible_pump_units_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=20|s=Page 20].

3. For general maintenance, suitable working tools and personal protective equipment should be used, and maintenance should be performed by qualified technicians [xylem_lowara_doc_iom_doc_submersible_pump_units_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=20|s=Page 20].

The documents do not list specific spare parts by name for DOC submersible pump maintenance beyond the supply cord and general advice on ordering parts via product codes. Therefore, the main parts needed are the supply cord (if damaged) and any other parts identified via the product codes on the official website or through the Authorized Distributor [xylem_lowara_doc_iom_doc_submersible_pump_units_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=20|s=Page 20].

6 Maintenance 
6.1 Precautions 
Before starting, make sure that the instructions shown in Introduction and Safety on page 4 
have been fully read and understood. 
WARNING: 
Maintenance must be done by a technician possessing the technical-professional requirements 
outlined in the current regulations. 
 
WARNING: 
Always wear personal protective equipment. 
 
WARNING: 
Always use suitable working tools. 
 
DANGER: Electrical hazard 
Before starting work, check that the unit is unplugged and that the pump unit, the control 
panel and the auxiliary control circuit cannot restart, even unintentionally. 
6.2 Maintenance every 6 months of operation 
1. Check the integrity of the supply cord; if the cable is damaged contact Xylem or the 
Authorised Distributor for its replacement. 
2. Carefully clean the unit, particularly near the suction port. 
6.3 Long periods of inactivity 
1. Rinse the unit with soft water. 
2. Empty the unit and the piping. 
3. Put the unit out of service. 
4. Protect the unit against freezing. 
6.4 Spare parts ordering 
Identify the spare parts with the product codes directly on the site www.lowara.com/spark. 
Contact Xylem or the Authorised Distributor for technical information.

Seal and Spacer Replacement
To replace seals and spacers, refer to Replacing Brine Valve,
Injectors and Screen, steps 1–3.
1.	 Remove the control valve back cover. Remove the control
valve front cover. Disconnect the meter dome signal wire
from the front cover and feed it back through the control.
2.	 Remove screw and washer at drive yoke. Remove timer
mounting screws. The entire timer assembly will now lift
off easily. Remove end plug retainer plate.
3.	 Pull upward on end of piston rod yoke until assembly is
out of valve. Remove and replace seals and spacers.
4.	 Take piston assembly and push piston into valve by
means of the end plug. Twist yoke carefully in a clockwise
direction to properly align it with drive gear. Replace end
plug retainer plate.
5.	 Place timer on top of valve. Be sure drive pin on main gear
engages slot in drive yoke.
6.	 Replace timer mounting screws. Replace screw and
washer at drive yoke.
7.	 Return bypass or inlet valve to normal In Service position.
Water pressure automatically builds in the conditioner.
NOTE:  	Be sure to shut off any bypass line.
8.	 Replace the control valve back cover.
9.	 Follow Injectors/Screen Replacement, steps 9–12.
Meter Replacement
To replace meter refer to Replacing Brine Valve, Injectors and
Screen, steps 1–3.
1.	 Remove two screws and clips at bypass valve or yoke. Pull
resin tank away from plumbing connections.
2.	 Pull meter module out of control valve.

Disassembly And Reassembly
DISASSEMBLY
Before working on pump or motor, lock
out driver power to prevent accidental
startup and physical injury.
NOTE: Pump components should be match-marked
prior to disassembly to ensure they are
reassembled in the correct location.
HEAD AND COLUMN
   1.	 On pumps which are driven through a gear drive,
remove the driveshaft between the gear and the
prime mover.
   2.	 On pumps, which are electric motor driven, remove
the electrical connections at the conduit box and tag
the electrical leads, so they can be reassembled the
same way they were disassembled.
   3.	 Uncouple driver (or gear box) from pump shaft and
mounting flanges and lift off by the lifting lugs or
eyebolts as furnished.
Never try to lift entire pump assembly by
the lifting lugs or eyebolts furnished for the
driver only.
   4.	 Disconnect discharge head from the discharge
piping. Remove all hold down bolts and external
piping. Remove coupling, packing box and proceed
with disassembly down to the bowls by reversing
the procedures described in detail for assembling the
unit.
BOWL ASSEMBLY
The bowl assembly is composed of a suction bowl/bell,
intermediate bowl(s), top bowl, impellers and securing
hardware, bearings, and pump shaft.
Turbine bowl impellers are secured to the shaft by either
a taperlock or a key and split thrust ring. Follow only
those procedures that apply to the particular construction
supplied.
NOTE: Match mark bowl assembly in sequence of
disassembly to aid in the reassembly procedure.

Seal and Spacer Replacement
To replace seals and spacers, refer to Replacing Brine Valve,
Injectors and Screen, steps 1–3.
1.	 Remove the control valve back cover. Remove the control
valve front cover. Disconnect the meter dome signal wire
from the front cover and feed it back through the control.
2.	 Remove screw and washer at drive yoke. Remove timer
mounting screws. The entire timer assembly will now lift
off easily. Remove end plug retainer plate.
3.	 Pull upward on end of piston rod yoke until assembly is
out of valve. Remove and replace seals and spacers.
4.	 Take piston assembly and push piston into valve by
means of the end plug. Twist yoke carefully in a clockwise
direction to properly align it with drive gear. Replace end
plug retainer plate.
5.	 Place timer on top of valve. Be sure drive pin on main gear
engages slot in drive yoke.
6.	 Replace timer mounting screws. Replace screw and
washer at drive yoke.
7.	 Return bypass or inlet valve to normal In Service position.
Water pressure automatically builds in the conditioner.
NOTE:  	Be sure to shut off any bypass line.
8.	 Replace the control valve back cover.
9.	 Follow Injectors/Screen Replacement, steps 9–12.
Meter Replacement
To replace meter refer to Replacing Brine Valve, Injectors and
Screen, steps 1–3.
1.	 Remove two screws and clips at bypass valve or yoke. Pull
resin tank away from plumbing connections.
2.	 Pull meter module out of control valve.

Disassembly And Reassembly
DISASSEMBLY
Before working on pump or motor, lock
out driver power to prevent accidental
startup and physical injury.
NOTE: Pump components should be match-marked
prior to disassembly to ensure they are
reassembled in the correct location.
HEAD AND COLUMN
   1.	 On pumps which are driven through a gear drive,
remove the driveshaft between the gear and the
prime mover.
   2.	 On pumps, which are electric motor driven, remove
the electrical connections at the conduit box and tag
the electrical leads, so they can be reassembled the
same way they were disassembled.
   3.	 Uncouple driver (or gear box) from pump shaft and
mounting flanges and lift off by the lifting lugs or
eyebolts as furnished.
Never try to lift entire pump assembly by
the lifting lugs or eyebolts furnished for the
driver only.
   4.	 Disconnect discharge head from the discharge
piping. Remove all hold down bolts and external
piping. Remove coupling, packing box and proceed
with disassembly down to the bowls by reversing
the procedures described in detail for assembling the
unit.
BOWL ASSEMBLY
The bowl assembly is composed of a suction bowl/bell,
intermediate bowl(s), top bowl, impellers and securing
hardware, bearings, and pump shaft.
Turbine bowl impellers are secured to the shaft by either
a taperlock or a key and split thrust ring. Follow only
those procedures that apply to the particular construction
supplied.
NOTE: Match mark bowl assembly in sequence of
disassembly to aid in the reassembly procedure.

INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.

1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.
3.	 All plumbing should be done in accordance with local
plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

[pentair_fleck_sxt_owners_manual_fleck_sxt_controllers_owner_s_manual.pdf|p=3|s=Page 3]
MANUAL OVERVIEW
How To Use This Manual
This owner’s manual is designed to provide the homeowner with instructions on performing routine care and 
maintenance of the residential water softener or filter valve and control packaged with this manual.
This manual does not include instructions regarding installation, setup, service, or troubleshooting of the 
valve, control, or other components of a residential water conditioning system. Please contact your local 
water treatment professional with questions or concerns about the operation or performance of your water 
conditioning system.
Icons That Appear In This Manual
WARNING:  Failure to follow this instruction can result in personal injury or damage to the equipment.
NOTE: This will make the process easier if followed. 
General Warnings
WARNING:   There are no user-serviceable parts in the AC adapter, motor, or controller. Do not attempt to 
remove or repair individual components.
WARNING:   Use only the power transformer supplied with this water conditioning system.
WARNING:   The power outlet must be grounded and always on. If it is necessary to disconnect power, 
unplug the AC adapter from its power source.
WARNING:   Only fill the brine tank with salt designed for water softening.
WARNING:   Ambient temperature surrounding the system should be between 35°F (1°C) and 120°F 
(49°C).
WARNING:   Water temperature flowing through the system should be between 35°F (1°F) and 100°F 
(38°C).
California Proposition 65 Warning
WARNING:  This product contains chemicals known to the State of California to cause cancer or birth 
defects or other reproductive harm.
Pentair Fleck SXT Controller Service Manual • 3

[pentair_fleck_sxt_owners_manual_fleck_sxt_controllers_owner_s_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4]
SETTING TIME OF DAY AND
INITIATING A MANUAL
REGENERATION
Setting the Time of Day
1.	 Press and hold either the Up or Down buttons until
the programming icon replaces the service icon and
the parameter display reads TD.
2.	 Adjust the displayed time with the Up and Down
buttons.
3.	 When the desired time is set, press the Extra Cycle
button to resume normal operation. The unit will
also return to normal operation after five seconds if
no buttons are pressed.
Queueing a Regeneration
1.	 Press the Extra Cycle button. The service icon will
flash to indicate that a regeneration is queued.
2.	 To cancel a queued regeneration, press the Extra
Cycle button.
Regenerating Immediately
Press and hold the Extra Cycle button for five seconds.
FEATURES OF THE PENTAIR FLECK SXT CONTROLLER
•	 Power backup that continues to keep time and the passage of days for a minimum of 8 hours in the event
of power failure. During a power outage, the control goes into a power-saving mode. It does not monitor
water usage during a power failure, but it does store the volume remaining at the time of power failure.
•	 Settings for both valve (basic system) and control type (method used to trigger a regeneration).
•	 Day-of-the-Week controls.
•	 While in service, the display alternates between time of day, volume remaining or days to regeneration,
and tank in service (twin tank systems only).
•	 The Flow Indicator flashes when outlet flow is detected.

raw_model_output:
The specifications and troubleshooting steps for the Fleck 5800 LXT valve are partially detailed in the service manual. For troubleshooting, if the unit does not measure flow, you should verify that the day override is set properly, the meter cable is connected properly, and that the meter is functioning properly. Additionally, you should enter Master Programming Mode and verify that the unit is configured appropriately for the valve configuration, and check that the correct system capacity and meter size have been selected. A specific error called "Fail Safe Error" (FSEr) indicates that the valve has failed to find position in one minute; the recommended step is to unplug the unit and plug it back in, and if the error continues, call technical support. Intended use
Circulating pump for domestic hot water systems.
If hot water is not used for longer periods of time, the water in the hot water pipe cools off.
Domestic hot water pumps (also called sanitary or drinking water circulating pumps) pump this
cold water back into the water heater via a separate recirculation pipe, or directly into the cold
water supply line (see Figure 5 and Figure 6 on page 19 and 20). At the same time fresh hot
water is flowing out of the water heater and provides a constant supply of hot water at the tap.
WARNING: Risk of electric shock
This pump has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas.
Do not install within an outer enclosure or beneath the skirt of a hot tub or spa.
This pump is not submersible.
CAUTION:
Acceptable for indoor use only. This pump has been evaluated for use with water only. Use with
maximum 203 °F (95 °C) water.
Pump selection
The e3-4 series models are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences with
a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m).
The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and
small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m).

Installation, Operation and Maintenance Manual
3.6
Intended use
Circulating pump for domestic hot water systems.
If hot water is not used for longer periods of time, the water in the hot water pipe cools off.
Domestic hot water pumps (also called sanitary or drinking water circulating pumps) pump this
cold water back into the water heater via a separate recirculation pipe, or directly into the cold
water supply line (see Figure 5 and Figure 6 on page 19 and 20). At the same time fresh hot
water is flowing out of the water heater and provides a constant supply of hot water at the tap.
WARNING: Risk of electric shock
This pump has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas.
Do not install within an outer enclosure or beneath the skirt of a hot tub or spa.
This pump is not submersible.
CAUTION:
Acceptable for indoor use only. This pump has been evaluated for use with water only. Use with
maximum 203 °F (95 °C) water.
Pump selection
The e3-4 series models are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences with
a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m).
The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and
small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m).

The installation requirements for the Fleck SXT controller include the following: The water pressure must be a minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) for the regeneration valve to operate effectively. The electrical supply must be an uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply, and the voltage supply should be compatible with the unit before installation. The existing plumbing should be free from lime and iron buildup; heavily built-up piping should be replaced, and if clogged with iron, a separate iron filter should be installed ahead of the water softener. The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air breaks and backflow. A bypass valve should always be provided if the unit is not equipped with one. Water pressure should not exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar), water temperature should not exceed 110°F (43°C), and the unit must not be subjected to freezing conditions. The unit should be placed level and on a firm base, and during cold weather, the valve should be warmed to room temperature before operating. All plumbing should comply with local plumbing codes, and the pipe size for residential drain lines should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm) [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4].

The reset and recovery procedure involves unplugging the unit, examining the powerhead, verifying all cam switches are connected and functioning properly, checking the motor and drive train components, and ensuring the piston travels freely. Components should be replaced or reassembled as necessary. After plugging the unit back in, it should cycle to the next valve position and stop. If the error recurs, unplug the unit and contact technical support.

- Error Code 1 (Cycle Step Error): This error indicates the control experienced an unexpected cycle input. The recovery steps include unplugging the unit, examining the powerhead, verifying cam switches, entering Master Programming mode to check valve and system type settings, manually stepping through a regeneration to verify function, and contacting technical support if the error persists.

- Error Code 2 (Regen Failure): This error means the system has not regenerated for more than 99 days (or 7 days if the Control Type is set to Day-of-Week). raw_model_output: To program the Fleck 5800 XTR2, you start by using the touchscreen control. When the unit is powered on, touch the screen to activate it. You can enter information such as the name and phone number of the water treatment professional or company for service by using the keypad on the screen. After entering the name and phone number, you can set the assistance interval, which determines when the homeowner will need to call for service. For softener systems, ensure to put salt in the brine tank, but do not use granulated or rock salt. Install MAG 5000 / MAG 6000 compact version 
1. Remove and discard terminal box lid of sensor. 
 
2. Ensure SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed. 
3. Fit M20 or ½" NPT cable glands for supply and output cables. 
4. Unplug the two black plug assemblies for coil and electrode cables in terminal box. 
5. Connect earth wire from connection board to bottom of terminal box. 
6. Connect 2-pin connector and 3-pin connector as shown to their corresponding terminal 
numbers on connection board as shown in Electrical connection (Page 36).

raw_model_output: If the Siemens MAG 6000 is vibrating excessively, Siemens recommends avoiding strong vibrations and suggests remote mounting of the transmitter in applications with strong vibrations. Therefore, you should investigate the mounting location and consider relocating the transmitter remotely to reduce the impact of vibrations. This can help mitigate issues related to vibrations affecting the device's performance [siemens_siemens_mag5100w_operating_instructions_sitrans_fm_mag_5100_w_operating_instructions.pdf|p=22|s=Page 22].

Start an Extra Regeneration Cycle

raw_model_output:
The regeneration procedure for the Fleck 5600 is as follows:

1. When the control is in service, press and hold the Extra Cycle button for five seconds on the main screen to manually initiate a regeneration.
2. The control advances to Regeneration Cycle Step #1 (backwash) and begins the programmed time countdown.
3. Press the Extra Cycle button once to advance the valve to Regeneration Cycle Step #2 (brine draw and slow rinse).
4. Press the Extra Cycle button once to advance the valve to Regeneration Cycle Step #3 (rapid rinse).
5. Press the Extra Cycle button once to advance the valve to Regeneration Cycle Step #4 (brine refill).
6. Press the Extra Cycle button once more to advance the valve back to in service.

Note: If the unit is a filter or upflow, the cycle step order may change. Also, pressing the Extra Cycle button during a regeneration cycle immediately advances the valve to the next cycle step position and resumes normal step timing. A queued regeneration can be initiated by pressing the Extra Cycle button, and to clear a queued regeneration, press the Extra Cycle button again to cancel. If regeneration occurs for any reason prior to the delayed regeneration time, the manual regeneration request will be cleared [pentair_fleck_5800lxt_service_manual_fleck_5800_lxt_downflow_upflow_service_manual.pdf|p=6|s=Page 6].

Hach SC200 controller is not responding, what are troubleshooting steps?

raw_model_output:
For troubleshooting the Hach SC200 controller when it is not responding, you can follow these steps:

1. Verify current output configuration if the issue is related to no current output.
2. Test the current output signal using the Test/Maintenance submenu.
3. Input a current value and verify the output signal at the controller connections.
4. Contact Technical Support if the problem persists.
5. For incorrect current output, verify the configuration and perform output calibration if needed.
6. For no relay activation, check relay connections, wiring, configuration, and test relay activation through the Test/Maintenance menu.
7. Ensure the controller is not in calibration mode and the relay is not being held.
8. Reset the Overfeed Timer if it has expired.
9. If the Secure Digital Memory (SD) card is not recognized, check the card orientation, seating, format (must be Fat 32), size (not larger than 32 GB), and type (must be SD card).
10. Follow the instructions of the card manufacturer to format the SD card on a PC if necessary.

These steps are summarized from the troubleshooting section of the SC200 user manual [hach_hach_sc200_user_manual_sc200_controller_basic_user_manual.pdf|p=26|s=Page 26].

For troubleshooting the Hach SC200 controller when it is not responding, you can follow these steps:

1. Verify current output configuration if the issue is related to no current output.
2. Test the current output signal using the Test/Maintenance submenu.
3. Input a current value and verify the output signal at the controller connections.
4. Contact Technical Support if the problem persists.
5. For incorrect current output, verify the configuration and perform output calibration if needed.
6. For no relay activation, check relay connections, wiring, configuration, and test relay activation through the Test/Maintenance menu.
7. Ensure the controller is not in calibration mode and the relay is not being held.
8. Reset the Overfeed Timer if it has expired.
9. If the Secure Digital Memory (SD) card is not recognized, check the card orientation, seating, format (must be Fat 32), size (not larger than 32 GB), and type (must be SD card).
10. Follow the instructions of the card manufacturer to format the SD card on a PC if necessary.

These steps are summarized from the troubleshooting section of the SC200 user manual [hach_hach_sc200_user_manual_sc200_controller_basic_user_manual.pdf|p=26|s=Page 26].

raw_model_output:
If the Fleck 7000SXT water conditioner fails to regenerate, you should check the following possible causes and apply the corresponding corrections:

- Ensure permanent electrical service by checking the fuse, plug, pull chain, or switch.
- Replace the timer if it is defective.
- Reset the time of day in case of power failure.
- Close the by-pass valve if it is open.
- Add salt to the brine tank and maintain the salt level above the water level if there is no salt.
- Clean the injector screen if it is plugged.
- Check the brine tank fill time and clean the brine line flow control if there is insufficient water flowing into the brine tank.
- Perform repeated flushings of the hot water tank if there is hardness in the hot water tank.
- Check that the distributor tube is not cracked and inspect the O-ring and tube pilot for leaks.
- Replace seals and spacers and/or piston if there is an internal valve leak.
- Check salt usage and salt setting if the unit used too much salt or has improper salt setting.
- Address excessive water in the brine tank as per the relevant instructions.
- Clean the line to the water conditioner if there is iron buildup causing loss of water pressure.
- Clean the control and add mineral cleaner to the mineral bed, and increase the frequency of regeneration if there is iron buildup in the water conditioner.
- Remove the piston and clean the control if the inlet of the control is plugged due to foreign material.
- Assure that the well system has proper air eliminator control and check for dry well condition if there is loss of mineral through the drain line.
- Verify that the drain line flow control is properly sized.

These steps are detailed in the troubleshooting section of the Fleck 7000SXT Service Manual. [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=17|s=Page 17]

- Close the by-pass valve if it is open.
- Add salt to the brine tank and maintain the salt level above the water level if there is no salt.
- Clean the injector screen if it is plugged.
- Check the brine tank fill time and clean the brine line flow control if there is insufficient water flowing into the brine tank.
- Perform repeated flushings of the hot water tank if there is hardness in the hot water tank.
- Check that the distributor tube is not cracked and inspect the O-ring and tube pilot for leaks.
- Replace seals and spacers and/or piston if there is an internal valve leak.
- Check salt usage and salt setting if the unit used too much salt or has improper salt setting.
- Address excessive water in the brine tank as per the relevant instructions.
- Clean the line to the water conditioner if there is iron buildup causing loss of water pressure.
- Clean the control and add mineral cleaner to the mineral bed, and increase the frequency of regeneration if there is iron buildup in the water conditioner.
- Remove the piston and clean the control if the inlet of the control is plugged due to foreign material.
- Assure that the well system has proper air eliminator control and check for dry well condition if there is loss of mineral through the drain line.
- Verify that the drain line flow control is properly sized.

These steps are detailed in the troubleshooting section of the Fleck 7000SXT Service Manual. [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=17|s=Page 17]

raw_model_output: The operating temperature range for Bell & Gossett e3-4 pumps depends on the certification of the model. In order to protect the electronics inside the pumps from temperatures that are dangerously
high, the pump is equipped with an internal temperature sensor and a self-protecting algorithm.
