raw_model_output:
To troubleshoot a Fleck SXT controller, you can refer to the error codes and their causes along with reset and recovery steps:

1. Error Code 0 - Cam Sense Error: This occurs when the valve drive takes longer than 6 minutes to advance to the next regeneration position. To reset, unplug the unit and check the powerhead, cam switches, motor, drive train components, and valve piston for proper function and assembly. Replace or reassemble components as needed. Plug the unit back in and observe if it cycles correctly. If the error persists, unplug and contact technical support.

2. Error Code 1 - Cycle Step Error: This happens when the control experiences an unexpected cycle input. Unplug the unit and check the powerhead and cam switches. Enter Master Programming mode to verify valve and system type settings. Manually step through a regeneration cycle to test functionality. If the error recurs, unplug and contact technical support.

3. Error Code 2 - Regen Failure: This indicates the system has not regenerated for more than 99 days (or 7 days if set to Day-of-Week). Perform a manual regeneration to reset the error. For metered systems, verify flow measurement by running service water and observing the flow indicator. Check day override, meter cable connection, meter function, and configuration settings in Master Programming Mode.

Additionally, general troubleshooting for water conditioner regeneration failure includes checking for electrical service interruptions, defective timer, power failure, open by-pass valve, no salt in brine tank, plugged injector screen, insufficient water flow into brine tank, leaks, internal valve leaks, improper salt settings, excessive water in brine tank, loss of water pressure, iron buildup, plugged inlet control, air in water system, and improperly sized drain line flow control. Corrective actions involve ensuring permanent electrical service, replacing timers, resetting time of day, closing by-pass valves, adding salt, cleaning screens and lines, checking for leaks, adjusting salt settings, cleaning mineral beds, and verifying proper air eliminators and drain line sizing.

For electrical issues, ensure the power adapter supplied with the system is used, connected to a constant power source (not a switched outlet), and that power interruptions longer than 8 hours may cause loss of time settings which must be re-entered when power is restored.

If errors continue after these steps, contact technical support for further assistance.

MANUAL OVERVIEW
How To Use This Manual
This owner’s manual is designed to provide the homeowner with instructions on performing routine care and 
maintenance of the residential water softener or filter valve and control packaged with this manual.
This manual does not include instructions regarding installation, setup, service, or troubleshooting of the 
valve, control, or other components of a residential water conditioning system. Please contact your local 
water treatment professional with questions or concerns about the operation or performance of your water 
conditioning system.
Icons That Appear In This Manual
WARNING:  Failure to follow this instruction can result in personal injury or damage to the equipment.
NOTE: This will make the process easier if followed. 
General Warnings
WARNING:   There are no user-serviceable parts in the AC adapter, motor, or controller. Do not attempt to 
remove or repair individual components.
WARNING:   Use only the power transformer supplied with this water conditioning system.
WARNING:   The power outlet must be grounded and always on. If it is necessary to disconnect power, 
unplug the AC adapter from its power source.
WARNING:   Only fill the brine tank with salt designed for water softening.
WARNING:   Ambient temperature surrounding the system should be between 35°F (1°C) and 120°F

query: What part do I need to replace piston seals on Fleck 9100?

assembled_prompt_messages.content: What part do I need to replace piston seals on Fleck 9100?

raw_model_output:
To replace piston seals on the Fleck 9100, you need the Seal & Spacer Kit for the upper piston and the Seal & Spacer Kit for the lower piston. Specifically, the part numbers are:

- Seal & Spacer Kit, 5600/9000/9100 Upper: Part No. 60125 (also available as 60125-15 Blue Silicone)
- Seal & Spacer Kit, 9000/9100 Lower: Part No. 60421 (also available as 60421-50 with 559PE seals)

These kits include the necessary seals and spacers for the piston assemblies on the Fleck 9100 control valve [p=14|s=Page 14].
returned_answer:
To replace piston seals on the Fleck 9100, you need the Seal & Spacer Kit for the upper piston and the Seal & Spacer Kit for the lower piston. Specifically, the part numbers are:

- Seal & Spacer Kit, 9000/9100 Lower: Part No. 60421 (also available as 60421-50 with 559PE seals)

7.7 
MAG 6000 SV 
Excitation frequency 
The MAG 6000 SV excitation frequency can be changed in sensor characteristics menu to 
one of the following frequencies: 
● 1 9/16 Hz 
● 3 1/8 Hz 
● 6 ¼ Hz 
● 12½ Hz 
● 25 Hz 
● 44 Hz 
 
Note 
Calibration has been made with the frequency stored in SENSORPROM® memory unit. A 
change in excitation frequency is not recommended and will always mean decreased 
measuring accuracy. In some instances, however, it may be necessary to change 
frequency due to pulsating flow from piston pumps or other resonance frequencies from 
surroundings. 
It is highly recommended to carry out a External input (Page 49) after changing the excitation 
frequency as the offset is affected by the frequency selected. When this is done, the 
decrease in measuring accuracy can be kept below 1% o.r. 
A too high frequency for the sensor used will cause a coil current alarm indication.

MAG 6000 SV 
Excitation frequency 
The MAG 6000 SV excitation frequency can be changed in sensor characteristics menu to 
one of the following frequencies: 
● 1 9/16 Hz 
● 3 1/8 Hz 
● 6 ¼ Hz 
● 12½ Hz 
● 25 Hz 
● 44 Hz 
 
Note 
Calibration has been made with the frequency stored in SENSORPROM® memory unit. A 
change in excitation frequency is not recommended and will always mean decreased 
measuring accuracy. In some instances, however, it may be necessary to change 
frequency due to pulsating flow from piston pumps or other resonance frequencies from 
surroundings. 
It is highly recommended to carry out a External input (Page 49) after changing the excitation 
frequency as the offset is affected by the frequency selected. When this is done, the 
decrease in measuring accuracy can be kept below 1% o.r. 
A too high frequency for the sensor used will cause a coil current alarm indication.

programming changes and return to normal operation if it is
left in Master Programming mode for 5 minutes without any

raw_model_output:
The provided documents do not contain specific instructions on how to configure the Fleck 9000 control. However, common issues and their corrections for the Fleck 9000/9100/9500 water conditioners are detailed as follows:

1. Water conditioner fails to regenerate:
   - Electrical service interrupted: Assure permanent electrical service by checking fuse, plug, pull chain, or switch.
   - Timer defective: Replace timer.
   - Power failure: Reset time of day.
   - Hard water: Close bypass valve if open.
   - No salt in brine tank: Add salt and maintain salt level above water level.
   - Injector screen plugged: Clean injector screen.
   - Insufficient water flowing into brine tank: Check brine tank fill time and clean brine line flow control if plugged.
   - Hot water tank hardness: Repeated flushings of the hot water tank required.
   - Leak at distributor tube: Check for cracks, O-ring, and tube pilot.
   - Internal valve leak: Replace seals, spacers, and/or piston.
   - Unit used too much salt: Check salt usage and salt setting.
   - Excessive water in brine tank: Refer to "Excessive water in brine tank" section.
   - Loss of water pressure.
   - Iron buildup in line or water conditioner: Clean line and control, add mineral cleaner, increase regeneration frequency.
   - Inlet of control plugged due to foreign material: Remove piston and clean control.
   - Loss of mineral through drain line.
   - Air in water system: Assure proper air eliminator control and check for dry well condition.
   - Improperly sized drain line flow control.

2. Softener delivers hard water:
   - Reserve capacity exceeded: Check salt dosage and reset program wheel for additional reserve.
   - Program wheel not rotating with meter output: Pull cable out of meter cover and rotate manually; replace timer if necessary.
   - Meter not measuring flow: Check meter with meter checker.

These issues and corrections provide guidance on troubleshooting common problems with the Fleck 9000 series water conditioners. For detailed configuration steps, please refer to the full service manual or contact technical support. Acceptance levels 
The following three acceptance levels are selectable.

Error information is displayed in title and subtitle lines, see display layout (Page 40). Title line 
will show time since occurrence of error in days, hours and minutes. Subtitle line will flash 
between an error text and a remedy text. Error text will indicate type of error (I, W, P or F), 
error number, and error text. Remedy text will inform operator of action to take to remove 
error. 
 
Status log 
The latest 9 errors are stored in the status log. Errors are stored in the status log for 180 
days, even if they are corrected. 
Alarm field 
The alarm field on the display will always flash when an error is pending. 
Error output 
The digital and relay output can be activated individually error by error (error level). The relay 
output is default selected to error level. An output can also be selected to activate on a single 
error number. 
The alarm field, error output and error pending always operate together.

Fleck 5600 is not responding, what are troubleshooting steps?

raw_model_output:
For troubleshooting a Fleck 5600 that is not responding, the following steps can be taken:

1. Check if the timer is cycling properly. If the timer is not cycling, replace the timer.
2. Inspect for any foreign material in the brine valve and clean or replace the brine valve seat if necessary.
3. Clean the brine line flow control if it is plugged.
4. Ensure the drain line flow control is not plugged and clean it if necessary.
5. Clean the injector and injector screen if they are plugged.
6. Verify that the line pressure is adequate; increase line pressure to at least 20 psi if it is too low.
7. Check for internal control leaks and replace seals, spacers, and piston assembly if needed.
8. Inspect the drive motor and switches to ensure the service adapter cycles properly.
9. Determine if any switch or timer is faulty and replace it or replace the complete power head if the control cycles continuously.
10. Check the timer program and positioning of the control if the drain flows continuously; replace the power head assembly if it is not positioning properly.
11. Remove the power head assembly and inspect the bore for foreign material; remove any foreign material and check the control in various regeneration positions.
12. Replace seals and piston assembly if there is an internal control leak.

These steps are summarized from the troubleshooting section for the Fleck 5600SXT Upflow Service Manual [p=20].

of residences with a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m). The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m). Because the system is pressurized, the number of floors in a home is not taken into consideration
in sizing the circulating pump. The pump has only to produce continuous flow at a pressure
sufficient to overcome the friction losses created by the piping in the house water supply line
and the return line.
NOTICE: Water pressure
A recirculating system is a pressurized system operating at the city water pressure, as
determined by the pressure regulator on your line, or by a well pump, if you are on a well system.
In most residential plumbing systems, water pressure is set at 35 psi (241 kPa) and above.
Below 35 psi (241 kPa), water pressure may not be sufficient to fill the pipe diameter, leaving
space for air to accumulate in the lines.
If your system pressure is less than 35 psi (241 kPa), use the next larger pump on the Pump
Selection Guide.
NOTICE: Oversized pumps
Pumps should not be so large as to produce flow rates that may eventually erode holes in the
pipes. According to the Copper Development Association, excessive erosion occurs at a velocity
of about 5 ft (1.5 m) per second and higher; or about 4 gpm (15 l/min) in 1/2" Type M copper
pipe.
Use the recommended recirculation line size shown in the Pump Selection Guide. The e3 series
pumps are sized so that flow velocities are below these limits.

Location of Softener and Drain

Always provide for the installation of a bypass valve if unit is not equipped with one.

query: What are the steps to calibrate Fleck SXT controller?
final_context_preview:
[pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=5|s=Page 5]
FLECK 7000SXT  Service Manual • 5
START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

number of days equal to the regeneration day override pass

regenerates the system at the programmed regeneration time
after the calculated system capacity is depleted. As with Meter
Immediate systems, the control calculates the system capacity
by dividing the unit capacity by the feedwater hardness and
subtracting the reserve. The reserve should be set to insure
that the system delivers treated water between the time the
system capacity is depleted and the actual regeneration time.
A Meter Delayed control will also start a regeneration cycle at
the programmed regeneration time if a number of days equal
to the regeneration day override pass before water usage
depletes the calculated system capacity.

START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

The Fleck  5800/5810/5812 XTRi Connected Valve can be paired 
with a smartphone or tablet. New users can download and install 
the Pentair Home App from the App Store or Google Play. WiFi 
connection must be 2.4 GHz.
Sign Up and Log In 
New users will need to create an account to monitor their water 
softeners. From the Log In page, press SIGN UP to create a new

Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.

making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.

room temperature before operating.

INSTALLATION
Water Pressure
A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is
required for regeneration valve to operate effectively.
Electrical Facilities
An uninterrupted alternating current (A/C) supply is required.
Note: Other voltages are available. Please make sure your
voltage supply is compatible with your unit before installation.
Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.
CAUTION  Water pressure is not to exceed 125 psi (8.6 bar),
water temperature is not to exceed 110°F (43°C),
and the unit cannot be subjected to freezing
conditions.
Installation Instructions
1.	 Place the softener tank where you want to install the unit
making sure the unit is level and on a firm base.
2.	 During cold weather, the installer should warm the valve to
room temperature before operating.

plumbing codes. The pipe size for residential drain line
should be a minimum of 1/2” (13 mm). Backwash flow

What is the startup sequence for DOC submersible pump?

raw_model_output:
The startup sequence for DOC submersible pump with a float switch version is as follows:

1. Connect the plug to the mains and/or turn on the switch. Depending on the position of the float, the unit will either stay idle or start to operate.
2. While the unit is in operation, check that:
   - No liquid is leaking from the pipes.
   - There is no unwanted noise or vibrations.
   - There are no vortexes near the suction port.
   - Liquid is actually being pumped.
3. When the float reaches the low position (minimum liquid level), the pump will automatically stop.

For versions without a float switch:
1. Connect the plug to the mains and/or turn on the switch; the unit will start.
2. Perform the same operational checks as for the float switch version.
3. Once the unit has pumped the liquid down to the minimum level, disconnect the plug from the mains and/or turn off the switch to stop the unit.

Additionally, to check the direction of rotation for three-phase motors:
1. Place the unit vertically on a level and flat surface.
2. Start and then immediately stop the unit while looking from the top. The rotation direction is correct if the unit's impulse movement at startup tends to turn it clockwise, indicating the motor is turning clockwise as it should.

These steps ensure proper startup and operation of the DOC submersible pump unit. Bell & Gossett e3-6 is vibrating excessively, what should I investigate?

raw_model_output:
For excessive vibrations in the Bell & Gossett e3-6 pump, you should investigate the following potential causes:

- Coupling misalignment
- Bent impeller unbalance
- Worn bearings
- Cavitation
- Piping strain
- Resonance

You may need to determine the cause using a shaft vibration frequency analyzer and/or disassemble the pump. This is a complex problem that may require factory service assistance. Additionally, check for motor or gear driveshaft end play maladjustment and straighten any bent shaft as per runout limits. Also, consider if the well is crooked and survey it, consulting the factory if necessary. These steps are recommended to address excessive vibrations effectively. Maximum Versatility
The SC200 controller allows the use of digital and analog 
sensors, either alone or in combination, to provide 
compatibility with Hach's broad range of sensors, eliminating

calibration procedures in 19 languages minimize complexity

transfer. Visual warning system provides critical alerts.

Installation, Operation and Maintenance Manual
3.6
Intended use
Circulating pump for domestic hot water systems.
If hot water is not used for longer periods of time, the water in the hot water pipe cools off.
Domestic hot water pumps (also called sanitary or drinking water circulating pumps) pump this
cold water back into the water heater via a separate recirculation pipe, or directly into the cold
water supply line (see Figure 5 and Figure 6 on page 19 and 20). At the same time fresh hot
water is flowing out of the water heater and provides a constant supply of hot water at the tap.
WARNING: Risk of electric shock
This pump has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas.
Do not install within an outer enclosure or beneath the skirt of a hot tub or spa.
This pump is not submersible.
CAUTION:
Acceptable for indoor use only. This pump has been evaluated for use with water only. Use with
maximum 203 °F (95 °C) water.
Pump selection
The e3-4 series models are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences with
a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m).
The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and
small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m).

Bell & Gossett e3-4 is vibrating excessively, what should I investigate?

raw_model_output:
If the Bell & Gossett e3-4 pump is vibrating excessively, you should investigate the following causes:

- Coupling misalignment, bent impeller unbalance, worn bearings, cavitation, piping strain, and/or resonance. This is a complex problem that may require factory service assistance.
- Motor or gear driveshaft end play maladjustment.
- Bent shaft, which should be straightened as required.
- Crooked well, which should be surveyed and the factory consulted.

Determining the cause may involve utilizing a shaft vibration frequency analyzer and/or disassembling the pump for inspection [xylem_goulds_water_technology_dwt_iom_deep_well_turbine_pumps_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=23|s=Page 23].

sources.text:
SC200™ UNIVERSAL CONTROLLER
Maximum Versatility
The SC200 controller allows the use of digital and analog 
sensors, either alone or in combination, to provide 
compatibility with Hach's broad range of sensors, eliminating 
the need for dedicated, parameter-speciﬁc controllers.
Ease of Use and Conﬁdence in Results
Large, high-resolution, transreﬂective display provides optimal 
viewing resolution in any lighting condition. Guided 
calibration procedures in 19 languages minimize complexity 
and reduce operator error. Password-protected SD card 
reader oﬀers a simple solution for data download and 
transfer. Visual warning system provides critical alerts.
Wide Variety of Communication Options
Utilize two to ﬁve analog outputs to transmit primary and 
secondary values for each sensor, or integrate Hach® sensors 
and analyzers into MODBUS RS232/RS485, Proﬁbus® DP, and 
HART networks.
One Controller for the Broadest Range of Sensors.
Choose from 30 digital and analog sensor families for up to 17 diﬀerent parameters.
Applications
• Drinking Water
• Wastewater
• Industrial Water
• Power
Password protected SD card reader offers a simple solution 
for data download and transfer, and SC200 and digital 
sensor conﬁguration ﬁle duplication and backup.

4 Installation
4.1
Precautions
Before starting, make sure that the safety instructions shown in section 1.2 Safety on page 4
have been fully read and understood.
DANGER: Potentially explosive atmosphere hazard
It is prohibited to start the unit in environments with potentially explosive atmospheres or with
combustible dusts.
WARNING:
Always wear personal protective equipment.
WARNING:
Always use suitable working tools.
WARNING:
When selecting the place of installation and connecting the unit to the hydraulic and electric
power supplies, strictly comply with current regulations.
WARNING:
Remove the unit from its packaging just before installation to prevent contamination from
external substances.
4.2
Installation area
• Only install in dry rooms where the pump and the piping is protected from freezing.
• Install in one of the permitted mounting positions (see Figure 8 on page 23).
• Observe the instructions given in the section 8.2 Operating environment on page 40.
WARNING: Risk of electric shock
This pump has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas.
Do not install within an outer enclosure or beneath the skirt of a hot tub or spa.
This pump is not submersible.
CAUTION:
Acceptable for indoor use only.
This pump has been evaluated for use with water only. Use with maximum 203 °F (95 °C) water.
WARNING: Hot surface hazard
If the pump, motor or piping are operating at extremely high or low temperature, guarding or
insulation is required.
CAUTION: Property damage hazard

raw_model_output:
The safety requirements for installing the Bell & Gossett e3-4 pump include the following:

1. Before starting installation, fully read and understand the safety instructions provided in section 1.2 Safety on page 4 of the manual.

2. Do not start the unit in environments with potentially explosive atmospheres or combustible dusts.

3. Always wear personal protective equipment and use suitable working tools.

4. When selecting the installation location and connecting the unit to hydraulic and electric power supplies, strictly comply with current regulations.

5. Remove the unit from its packaging just before installation to prevent contamination from external substances.

6. Install the pump only in dry rooms where the pump and piping are protected from freezing.

7. Install the pump in one of the permitted mounting positions as specified in the manual.

8. The pump is for indoor use only and has been evaluated for use with water only, with a maximum temperature of 203 °F (95 °C).

9. The pump has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas and is not submersible. Do not install within an outer enclosure or beneath the skirt of a hot tub or spa.

10. If the pump, motor, or piping operate at extremely high or low temperatures, guarding or insulation is required to prevent hot surface hazards.

11. Electrical connections must be made by a qualified electrician in accordance with all applicable codes and ordinances.

12. Disconnect and lock out power before making electrical connections and ensure the unit cannot restart unintentionally.

13. Use wires acceptable for at least 194 °F (90 °C) and copper conductors only.

14. Connect only to a branch circuit protected by a ground-fault circuit-interrupter (GFCI) and test the GFCI routinely.

15. Adequate electrical grounding is required for safe operation.

16. Replace damaged cords immediately to reduce the risk of electric shock.

17. The pump is supplied with a grounding conductor and grounding-type attachment plug; connect only to a properly grounded, grounding-type receptacle.

18. To reduce the risk of injury, do not permit children to use the product unless closely supervised.

These requirements ensure safe installation and operation of the Bell & Gossett e3-4 pump system. 4.3 MAG 5000/6000 compact 
 
SITRANS F M MAG 5000/6000 
22 
Operating Instructions, 12/2013, A5E02338368-002 
4.3 
MAG 5000/6000 compact 
Install MAG 5000 / MAG 6000 compact version 
1. Remove and discard terminal box lid of sensor. 
 
2. Ensure SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed. 
3. Fit M20 or ½" NPT cable glands for supply and output cables. 
4. Unplug the two black plug assemblies for coil and electrode cables in terminal box. 
5. Connect earth wire from connection board to bottom of terminal box. 
6. Connect 2-pin connector and 3-pin connector as shown to their corresponding terminal 
numbers on connection board as shown in Electrical connection (Page 36). 
 
Note 
System will not register flow if black plugs are not connected to connection board. 
 
7. Fit supply and output cables through cable glands and connect to connection plate as 
shown in Electrical connection (Page 36).

How do I configure Siemens MAG 5000 and what are common issues?

raw_model_output:
To configure the Siemens MAG 5000, you should follow the installation and mounting instructions specific to the MAG 5000/6000 compact or CT versions. For the compact version, the steps include removing the terminal box lid, ensuring the SENSORPROM® memory unit is installed, fitting cable glands, connecting coil and electrode cables, connecting the earth wire, and connecting supply and output cables as per the electrical connection guidelines (Page 24). For the CT version, after tightening cable glands and connecting the power supply PE wire and coil cable shield correctly, mount the transmitter on the terminal box and power it up (Page 24, 30).

Regarding common issues, troubleshooting guidance includes checking for power supply problems if the display is empty, ensuring current and digital outputs are enabled if no flow signal is detected, and verifying cable connections if error codes such as F70 (incorrect or no coil current) or P42 (no load on current output) appear. Other issues include unstable flow signals caused by pulsating flow, low conductivity, electrical noise, air bubbles, or high particle concentration, which can be addressed by adjusting settings or ensuring proper installation. Additionally, errors like P40 indicate no SENSORPROM® unit installed, and P44 relates to SENSORPROM® unit issues requiring replacement or reset (Page 63).

For detailed configuration and troubleshooting, refer to the respective sections in the operating instructions and contact Siemens Technical Support if needed (Page 60).

What are the safety warnings in the DOC submersible pump manual?

raw_model_output:
The safety warnings in the DOC submersible pump manual include the following:

- Danger levels and safety symbols are used to indicate the severity of hazards. "DANGER" identifies a dangerous situation which, if not avoided, causes serious injury or death. "WARNING" identifies a dangerous situation which may cause serious injury or death. "CAUTION" identifies a situation which may cause small or medium level injuries. "NOTICE" identifies a situation which may cause damage to the product or unit malfunction. Users must read, understand, and comply with these warnings to avoid injuries, health hazards, product damage, or malfunction [Document 1, p.4].

- Electrical hazards: Do not use the unit in swimming pools or similar places when people are inside. Using the unit outdoors with a cable less than 10 m (32 ft) long is forbidden. Check that the unit is properly connected to the mains power supply [Document 5, p.18].

- Injuries hazard: Do not insert your hands at the bottom of the unit when in operation due to risk of personal injury caused by moving components. The unit, equipped with a single-phase motor with automatic reset thermal overload protection, could restart inadvertently after it has cooled down, posing a risk of physical injury. It is prohibited to put combustible materials near the unit. Do not hold the unit by the handle during operation. Make sure that the drained liquid cannot cause damage or injuries [Document 5, p.18].

- Dry run of the unit is forbidden. Make sure that the suction port is completely submerged in the liquid before start-up. The unit may only operate for a few minutes while only partially submerged in the liquid, for example during emptying operations [Document 5, p.18].

- Installation precautions include not starting the unit in environments with potentially explosive atmospheres or combustible dusts. Always wear personal protective equipment and use suitable working tools. When selecting the installation place and connecting the unit to hydraulic and electric power supplies, strictly comply with current regulations. Remove the unit from its packaging just before installation to prevent contamination [Document 4, p.17].

- The pump is not submersible and has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas. It is acceptable for indoor use only and has been evaluated for use with water only, with a maximum temperature of 203 °F (95 °C). If the pump, motor, or piping operate at extremely high or low temperatures, guarding or insulation is required [Document 4, p.17].

These warnings and precautions are essential to ensure safe installation, operation, and maintenance of the DOC submersible pump units [Documents 1, 4, 5].

caused by moving components. 
 
WARNING: Injuries hazard 
The unit, equipped with a single-phase motor with automatic reset thermal overload 
protection, could restart inadvertently after it has cooled down: risk of physical injury. 
 
WARNING: 
It is prohibited to put combustible materials near the unit. 
 
WARNING: 
Do not hold the unit by the handle during operation. 
 
WARNING: 
Make sure that the drained liquid cannot cause damage or injuries. 
 
NOTICE: 
Dry run of the unit is forbidden. 
 
NOTICE: 
Make sure that the suction port is completely submerged in the liquid before start-up. 
 
NOTICE: 
The unit may only operate for a few minutes while only partially submerged in the liquid, for 
example during emptying operations.

How do I troubleshoot Siemens MAG 5000?

raw_model_output:
To troubleshoot the Siemens MAG 5000, follow these steps based on the symptoms and error codes:

1. If the display is empty and output signals are minimum:
   - Check for power supply issues.
   - Inspect the MAG 5000/6000 for bent pins on the connector.
   - If defective, replace the MAG 5000/6000.

2. If there is no flow signal and output signals are minimum:
   - Ensure current output and digital output are enabled.
   - Check for reverse flow direction and correct it.
   - Error codes like F70 indicate incorrect or no coil current; check cables and connections.
   - W31 means the measuring pipe is empty; ensure it is full.
   - F60 indicates an internal error; replace the MAG 5000/6000.

3. For undefined errors such as P42 and P41:
   - P42 may mean no load on current output or defective MAG 5000/6000; check cables or replace device.
   - P41 indicates an initializing error; switch off the device for 5 seconds and switch on again.

4. If the device indicates flow with no flow in the pipe:
   - Select empty pipe cut-off or ensure the measuring pipe is full.
   - Check electrode connection and ensure the electrode cable is sufficiently screened.

5. For unstable flow signals:
   - Increase the time constant if pulsating flow or high concentration of particles/fibers.
   - Use special electrode cable if conductivity is too low.
   - Ensure sufficient potential equalization to avoid electrical noise.
   - Remove air bubbles from the medium.

6. For measuring errors:
   - Check installation correctness.
   - Ensure SENSORPROM® unit is installed; error code P40 indicates missing SENSORPROM®.
   - Replace or reset SENSORPROM® unit if error code P44 appears.

7. Additional error codes:
   - F63: Defective SENSORPROM® unit; replace it.
   - F71: Loss of internal data; replace MAG 5000/6000.
   - W30: Flow exceeds 100% of Qmax; check Qmax settings.
   - W21: Pulse overflow; adjust volume/pulse or pulse width.
   - W20: Initializing error; reset totalizer manually.

8. If unstable or wrong measurements occur, check earthing and potential equalization. If earthing is OK, check the transmitter and sensor according to their checklists.

9. If no replacement transmitter is available, check the transmitter by powering it on and observing the display and output readings. Replace display or transmitter if defective.

For detailed error codes, causes, and remedies, refer to the troubleshooting tables in the operating instructions.

If further technical support is needed, contact Siemens Technical Support via their internet support request or phone.

Note: Repair and service must be carried out by approved Siemens personnel only.

This summary is based on the troubleshooting and service instructions provided in the Siemens MAG 5000/6000 operating instructions. [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=59|p=60|p=61|p=62|p=63|p=64]

raw_model_output:
Low pressure in a Fleck 9100 water conditioner can be caused by several issues according to the service manual. Possible causes include:

- Loss of water pressure itself.
- Iron buildup in the line to the water conditioner.
- Iron buildup inside the water conditioner.
- Inlet of control plugged due to foreign material broken loose from pipes by recent plumbing work.

The recommended corrections are to clean the line to the water conditioner, clean the control and add mineral cleaner to the mineral bed, and remove the piston and clean the control if the inlet is plugged. These steps should help restore proper pressure and function to the unit. Additionally, checking for leaks at the distributor tube and ensuring the O-ring and tube pilot are intact is advised. If internal valve leaks are suspected, replacing seals, spacers, and/or the piston may be necessary. Ensuring the bypass valve is closed and that there is no air in the water system can also help maintain proper pressure. However, general troubleshooting and service hints for Fleck 9000/9100/9500 models include checking and correcting issues such as electrical service interruptions, timer defects, salt levels in the brine tank, injector screen cleanliness, water pressure, and internal valve leaks. Maintenance actions may involve assuring permanent electrical service, replacing the timer if defective, adding salt to the brine tank, cleaning the injector screen, checking and cleaning the brine line flow control, inspecting the distributor tube for leaks, replacing seals and spacers if there is an internal valve leak, and cleaning the control and mineral bed if iron buildup is present. Troubleshooting- NXT2 Controller Error Codes
Error Codes and Troubleshooting
Detected Errors
If a communication error is detected, an Error Screen will appear.
• All units In Service remain in the In Service position.
• All units in Standby go to In Service.
• Any unit in Regeneration when the error occurs completes
Regeneration and goes to In Service.
• No units are allowed to start a Regeneration Cycle while the
error condition exists, unless they are manually forced into
Regeneration.
• When an error is corrected and the error no longer displays
(it may take several seconds for all of the units in a system to
stop displaying the error message), the system returns to
normal operation.
NOTE:  During the error condition, the control continues
to monitor the flow meter and update the volume remain-
ing. Once the error condition is corrected, all units return
to the operating status they were in prior to the error.
Regeneration queue is rebuilt according to the normal sys-
tem operation. Or, if more than one unit has been queued
for regeneration, then the queue is rebuilt according to
which one communicates first.

Hach SC200 controller error indicator is on, what does this mean?

raw_model_output: The Hach SC200 controller has a visual warning system that provides critical alerts when the error indicator is on. This means there is a critical alert or error condition that requires attention to ensure proper operation of the controller and connected sensors. The exact nature of the error would need to be identified through the controller's display or diagnostic menus to determine the appropriate corrective action. The visual warning system is designed to help users quickly recognize when there is an issue with the controller or sensors [hach_hach_sc200_product_literature_sc200_universal_controller_literature.pdf|p=1|s=Page 1].

If a communication error is detected, an Error Screen will appear.
• All units In Service remain in the In Service position.

normal operation.

START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

FLECK 7000SXT  Service Manual • 5
START-UP INSTRUCTIONS
The water softener should be installed with the inlet,
outlet, and drain connections made in accordance with the
manufacturer’s recommendations, and to meet applicable
plumbing codes.
1.	 Turn the manual regeneraton knob slowly in a clockwise
direction until the program micro switch lifts on top of the
first set of pins. Allow the drive motor to move the piston
to the first regeneration step and stop. Each time the
program switch position changes, the valve will advance to
the next regeneration step. Always allow the motor to stop
before moving to the next set of pins or spaces.
NOTE:  	For electronic valves, please refer to the manual
regeneration part of the timer operation section.
If the valve came with a separate electronic timer
service manual, refer to the timer operation section
of the electronic timer service manual.
2.	 Position the valve to backwash. Ensure the drain line flow
remains steady for 10 minutes or until the water runs clear
(see above).
3.	 Position the valve to the brine / slow rinse position. Ensure
the unit is drawing water from the brine tank (this step may
need to be repeated).
4.	 Position the valve to the rapid rinse position. Check the
drain line flow, and run for 5 minutes or until the water
runs clear.
5.	 Position the valve to the start of the brine tank fill cycle.
Ensure water goes into the brine tank at the desired rate.

raw_model_output: When the Fleck 5800 SXT error indicator is on, it means there is an error condition detected by the system. The error codes appear on the In Service display and indicate specific issues such as Cam Sense Error, Cycle Step Error, Regen Failure, Memory Error, or Upper Drive Sync issues. For example, a Regen Failure error means the system has not regenerated for more than 99 days (or 7 days if the Control Type is set to Day-of-Week), and a manual regeneration is required to reset the error code. Other errors may require checking the powerhead, cam switches, motor, drive train components, or performing a Master Reset and reconfiguration. If the error persists after troubleshooting, contacting technical support is advised. Additionally, if the display is in sleep mode when an error occurs, the screen will turn on for five minutes and beep until the error is cleared, then switch to power saving mode displaying the Error Alert button as a screen saver [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=18|s=Page 18][pentair_fleck_5800xtr2_service_manual_fleck_5800_xtr2_service_manual.pdf|p=17|s=Page 17][pentair_fleck_5800sxt_service_manual_fleck_5800_sxt_downflow_upflow_service_manual.pdf|p=15|s=Page 15].

Siemens MAG 6000 is not responding, what are troubleshooting steps?

raw_model_output:
If the Siemens MAG 6000 is not responding, the following troubleshooting steps can be taken:

1. Check for power supply issues:
   - Verify that the MAG 5000/6000 has power supply.
   - Check for bent pins on the connector.
   - If defective, replace the MAG 5000/6000.

2. Check cables and connections:
   - Inspect cables and connections for any faults.
   - Check the connection board and pins in the transmitter multiplug.

3. Verify output signals:
   - Ensure current output and digital output are enabled.
   - If no flow signal, check for reverse flow direction and correct it.

4. Check for error codes and their remedies:
   - F70: Incorrect or no coil current - check cables/connections.
   - W31: Measuring pipe empty - ensure the measuring pipe is full.
   - F60: Internal error - replace MAG 5000/6000.
   - P42: No load on current output - check cables/connections or replace MAG 5000/6000.
   - P41: Initializing error - switch off MAG 5000/6000, wait 5 seconds, and switch on again.
   - F63: Defective SENSORPROM unit - replace SENSORPROM unit.
   - F71: Loss of internal data - replace MAG 5000/6000.

5. Check installation and sensor:
   - Verify correct installation.
   - Ensure SENSORPROM unit is installed.
   - Check electrode connections and cable screening.

6. If the display is empty but the transmitter is OK, check the display and replace if defective.

7. If the transmitter is defective, replace the transmitter.

8. For further technical support, contact Siemens Technical Support via their internet support request or phone.

Note: Repair and service must be carried out by approved Siemens Flow Instruments personnel only. Sensors are defined as non-repairable products by Siemens Flow Instrument.

These steps are summarized from the troubleshooting and technical support sections for the SITRANS F M MAG 5000/6000 devices [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=60|p=61|p=63|p=64].

raw_model_output:
The setup steps for the Lowara DOC pump include the following:

1. Place the unit in the vertical position on a level and flat surface.
2. Check the direction of rotation for three-phase motors by starting and then immediately stopping the unit while looking at it from the top. The rotation direction is correct if the unit impulse movement at start-up tends to turn it clockwise.
3. For the float switch version:
   - Connect the plug to the mains and/or turn on the switch. Depending on the float position, the unit will either stay idle or start to operate.
   - While the unit is operating, check that no liquid is leaking from the pipes, there is no unwanted noise or vibrations, there are no vortexes near the suction port, and liquid is actually being pumped.
   - The pump will automatically stop when the float reaches the low position (minimum liquid level).
4. For the version without a float switch:
   - Connect the plug to the mains and/or turn on the switch to start the unit.
   - Perform the same operational checks as for the float switch version.
   - Once the unit has taken up liquid to the minimum level, disconnect the plug from the mains and/or turn off the switch to stop it.

Additionally, the float switch controls the start and stop of the unit, and the level difference between start and stop can be adjusted by changing the length of the float cable using the cable stop on the handle. A shorter cable decreases the distance between minimum and maximum levels, causing more frequent starts and stops, while a longer cable increases the distance, causing less frequent starts and stops. The minimum and maximum permitted levels for operation depend on the model of the pump.

All hydraulic and electrical connections must be completed by a qualified technician, and the external protection conductor (ground) must always be connected before making any other electrical connections. Before starting work, ensure the unit is unplugged and cannot restart unintentionally.

These steps ensure proper setup and safe operation of the Lowara DOC pump unit. Error Codes and Troubleshooting
Detected Errors
If a communication error is detected, an Error Screen will appear.
• All units In Service remain in the In Service position.
• All units in Standby go to In Service.
• Any unit in Regeneration when the error occurs completes
Regeneration and goes to In Service.
• No units are allowed to start a Regeneration Cycle while the
error condition exists, unless they are manually forced into
Regeneration.
• When an error is corrected and the error no longer displays
(it may take several seconds for all of the units in a system to
stop displaying the error message), the system returns to
normal operation.
NOTE:  During the error condition, the control continues
to monitor the flow meter and update the volume remain-
ing. Once the error condition is corrected, all units return
to the operating status they were in prior to the error.
Regeneration queue is rebuilt according to the normal sys-
tem operation. Or, if more than one unit has been queued
for regeneration, then the queue is rebuilt according to
which one communicates first.

query: How do I program Fleck 9000?
final_context_preview:
[pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4]
4 • FLECK
® 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual
19210 Rev D
Figure 5  Program Wheel
19.	Cycle timer into backwash position. Turn manual knob so
that the micro switch rides on the first set of pins. In this
position the tanks switch (lower piston) and the control
valve moves to the backwash position (upper piston). Wait
until the positioning of upper and lower pistons stops
before advancing the timer further. If advanced too fast
the control will not home into the In Service position (it
will not advance to any other position). To correct this,
rotate the manual knob back to In Service and start again
into backwash.
NOTE:  	Once valve positions itself into the backwash cycle,
the homing circuit locks in.
20.	With all the air backwashed, slowly cycle the timer to the
brine position; rapid rinse; and brine tank refill. Wait for
the control drive motor to position itself in each cycle and
stop, before advancing on to the next position.
21.	Once back in the In Service position, cycle the control
valve again into the backwash position. The tanks switch
again, and air head backwashes out of the other tank.
Cycle the control back to the In Service position. Leave the
timer in the open position. DO NOT insert meter cable yet.
NOTE:  	Two motors are available.
1/15 RPM has 82 minute regeneration time.
1/30 RPM has 164 minute regeneration time.
Valve To Tank Installation
1.	 Spin the valve onto the tank, ensuring the threads are not
cross-threaded.

[pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=36|s=Page 36]
36 • FLECK
® 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual
GENERAL SERVICE HINTS FOR METER 
CONTROL
Problem: Softener delivers hard water
Reason: Reserve capacity has been exceeded. 
Correction: Check salt dosage requirements and reset 
program wheel to provide additional reserve.
Reason: Program wheel is not rotating with meter output.
Correction: Pull cable out of meter cover and rotate manually. 
Program wheel must move without binding and clutch must 
give positive clicks when program wheel strikes regeneration 
stop. If it does not, replace timer.
Reason: Meter is not measuring flow.
Correction: Check meter with meter checker.

How do I program Fleck 9000?

raw_model_output:
To program the Fleck 9000, you need to use the program wheel and follow the cycle timer steps carefully. First, cycle the timer into the backwash position by turning the manual knob so that the micro switch rides on the first set of pins. Wait until the positioning of the upper and lower pistons stops before advancing the timer further. If advanced too fast, the control will not home into the In Service position and will not advance to any other position. To correct this, rotate the manual knob back to In Service and start again into backwash. Once the valve positions itself into the backwash cycle, the homing circuit locks in. Then, slowly cycle the timer to the brine position, rapid rinse, and brine tank refill, waiting for the control drive motor to position itself in each cycle and stop before advancing to the next position. Finally, once back in the In Service position, cycle the control valve again into the backwash position to backwash air head out of the other tank, then cycle back to In Service and leave the timer in the open position without inserting the meter cable yet. Note that two motors are available with different regeneration times (1/15 RPM with 82 minutes and 1/30 RPM with 164 minutes) [pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4].

Additionally, the Fleck 9000 uses a program wheel assembly which is part of the timer housing and includes components such as the clutch, actuator, and micro switches. The program wheel must move without binding and the clutch must give positive clicks when the program wheel strikes the regeneration stop. If the program wheel does not rotate with the meter output, you should pull the cable out of the meter cover and rotate manually to check. If it does not function properly, the timer may need to be replaced [pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4; pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=36|s=Page 36].

For detailed programming options such as setting the time of day, regeneration time, feed water hardness, reserve capacity, and current day, these are typically accessed through user or master programming modes on other Fleck models like the 7000SXT or 5810/5812SXT, but specific instructions for the Fleck 9000 programming interface are not detailed in the provided documents. However, the program wheel and manual knob are the primary means of programming the Fleck 9000 control valve [pentair_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual_fleck_7000sxt_service_manual.pdf|p=8|s=Page 8; pentair_fleck_5810_5812sxt_manual_fleck_5810_5812_sxt_manual.pdf|p=6|s=Page 6].

Therefore, programming the Fleck 9000 involves manual cycling of the program wheel through the regeneration steps and ensuring the mechanical components operate correctly as described above.

The Siemens MAG 6000 requires a mains supply of 115 ... 230 V AC from building installation Class II. For DC installations, it is recommended to install an under voltage relay or protection circuit in applications where there is a risk of low power supply below the specifications for more than 10 minutes. Additionally, the mains protective earth wire must be connected to the PE terminal in accordance with the diagram due to class 1 power supply requirements. If a mechanical counter is connected to terminals 57 and 58 (active output), a 1000 µF capacitor must be connected (capacitor+ to terminal 56 and capacitor- to terminal 58). Output cables should be screened if long cables are used in noisy environments. For digital output, if the internal resistance of a load exceeds 10 kΩ, an external 10 kΩ load resistor should be connected in parallel to this load. Intrinsically safe terminals require that the distance between cables/wires is at least 50 mm to avoid contact between intrinsically safe circuits and other cables, and cables/wires should be fastened to prevent contact even in case of an error. Wire ends should be kept as short as possible [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=39|s=Page 39].

numbers on connection board as shown in Electrical connection (Page 36).

Acceptance levels 
The following three acceptance levels are selectable. 
● Fatal error: Only fatal errors are registered as errors 
● Permanent error: Permanent and fatal errors are registered as errors 
● Warning (Default value): Warnings, permanent and fatal errors are registered as errors 
Error information is displayed in title and subtitle lines, see display layout (Page 40). Title line 
will show time since occurrence of error in days, hours and minutes. Subtitle line will flash 
between an error text and a remedy text. Error text will indicate type of error (I, W, P or F), 
error number, and error text. Remedy text will inform operator of action to take to remove 
error. 
 
Status log 
The latest 9 errors are stored in the status log. Errors are stored in the status log for 180 
days, even if they are corrected. 
Alarm field 
The alarm field on the display will always flash when an error is pending. 
Error output 
The digital and relay output can be activated individually error by error (error level). The relay 
output is default selected to error level. An output can also be selected to activate on a single 
error number. 
The alarm field, error output and error pending always operate together. 
Operator menu

) in the operator menu.

- WARNING indicates that death or severe personal injury may result if proper precautions are not taken.
- CAUTION indicates that minor personal injury can result if proper precautions are not taken.
- NOTICE indicates that property damage can result if proper precautions are not taken.

If more than one degree of danger is present, the warning notice representing the highest degree of danger will be used. A notice warning of injury to persons with a safety alert symbol may also include a warning relating to property damage. The manual emphasizes that the product/system may be operated only by qualified personnel who are capable of identifying risks and avoiding potential hazards when working with these products/systems. Additionally, Siemens products may only be used for the applications described in the catalog and relevant technical documentation, and proper transport, storage, installation, assembly, commissioning, operation, and maintenance are required to ensure safe operation. The permissible ambient conditions must be complied with, and the information in the relevant documentation must be observed [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=4|s=Page 4][siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=8|s=Page 8].

For installation in hazardous locations, the equipment must be Ex-approved and marked accordingly. Special conditions for safe use provided in the manual and in the Ex certificate must be followed. The device complies with several directives including EMC-guideline 89/336/EEC, Low voltage guideline 73/23/EWG, ATEX Directive 94/9/EG, and others. Electrical connections must comply with specific standards such as Elex V and EN60079-14. Protective covers over the power supply must be properly installed, and for intrinsically safe circuits, the connection area can be opened. Appropriate cable connectors must be used for output circuits (blue for intrinsically safe, black for non-intrinsically safe). Sensor and transmitter must be connected to potential equalization, which must be maintained along the entire connection path for intrinsically safe output circuits. Sensor insulation thickness is limited to a maximum of 100mm for insulated sensors. When protective earth (PE) is connected, no potential difference between PE and potential equalization (PA) can exist, even during a fault condition [siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=14|s=Page 14][siemens_siemens_mag5000_mag6000_operating_instructions_sitrans_f_m_mag_5000_6000_operating_instructions.pdf|p=15|s=Page 15].

the pump must be cleaned before it is returned.

stored. It is essential that there are no traces of toxic or
hazardous media remaining on the pump.

declaration at the end of these instructions must be filled in by

position.

health or toxic. If the pump has been used for such substances,
the pump must be cleaned before it is returned.

A minimum of 20 pounds (1.4 bar) of water pressure is

Existing Plumbing
Condition of existing plumbing should be free from lime and
iron buildup. Piping that is built up heavily with lime and/
or iron should be replaced. If piping is clogged with iron, a
separate iron filter unit should be installed ahead of the water
softener.
Location Of Softener And Drain
The softener should be located close to a drain to prevent air
breaks and back flow.
By-Pass Valves
Always provide for the installation of a by-pass valve if unit is
not equipped with one.

MANUAL OVERVIEW
How To Use This Manual
This owner’s manual is designed to provide the homeowner with instructions on performing routine care and 
maintenance of the residential water softener or filter valve and control packaged with this manual.
This manual does not include instructions regarding installation, setup, service, or troubleshooting of the 
valve, control, or other components of a residential water conditioning system. Please contact your local 
water treatment professional with questions or concerns about the operation or performance of your water 
conditioning system.
Icons That Appear In This Manual
WARNING:  Failure to follow this instruction can result in personal injury or damage to the equipment.
NOTE: This will make the process easier if followed. 
General Warnings
WARNING:   There are no user-serviceable parts in the AC adapter, motor, or controller. Do not attempt to 
remove or repair individual components.
WARNING:   Use only the power transformer supplied with this water conditioning system.
WARNING:   The power outlet must be grounded and always on. If it is necessary to disconnect power, 
unplug the AC adapter from its power source.
WARNING:   Only fill the brine tank with salt designed for water softening.
WARNING:   Ambient temperature surrounding the system should be between 35°F (1°C) and 120°F 
(49°C).
WARNING:   Water temperature flowing through the system should be between 35°F (1°F) and 100°F 
(38°C).
California Proposition 65 Warning
WARNING:  This product contains chemicals known to the State of California to cause cancer or birth

5.2 Checking the direction of rotation (three-phase motors) 
1. Place the unit in the vertical position on a level and flat surface.

To install a Lowara DOC pump, follow these steps:

1. Ensure that all hydraulic and electrical connections are completed by a technician with the required technical-professional qualifications according to current regulations. Before starting work, verify that the unit is unplugged and that the pump unit, control panel, and auxiliary control circuit cannot restart unintentionally. Always connect the external protection conductor (ground) to the ground terminal before making any other electrical connections to avoid electrical hazards. (Document 5, p.16)

2. Position the pump unit properly in the system, typically involving components such as a gate valve, check valve, tank, float, electric supply cord, discharge pipe, and the pump unit itself as shown in the typical installation figure. (Document 5, p.16)

3. For electrical connection, ensure compliance with safety regulations and grounding requirements as mentioned above. (Document 5, p.16)

4. After installation, check the direction of rotation for three-phase motors by placing the unit vertically on a level surface, starting and immediately stopping it, and confirming that the impulse movement tends to turn clockwise, indicating correct motor rotation. (Document 1, p.19)

5. For starting and stopping, if the pump has a float switch, connect the plug to the mains or turn on the switch; the unit will start or stay idle depending on the float position. Check for leaks, noise, vibrations, vortexes near the suction port, and confirm liquid is being pumped. The pump stops automatically when the float reaches the low position. For versions without a float switch, connect the plug or turn on the switch to start, perform the same checks, and switch off when the liquid reaches minimum level. (Document 1, p.19)

6. Follow all safety precautions and wear personal protective equipment during installation. (Document 6, p.17)

These steps provide a general guideline for installing the Lowara DOC pump safely and correctly. (Documents 1, 5, 6)

It is prohibited to use the unit to pump flammable and/or explosive liquids, and it is also prohibited to start the unit in environments with potentially explosive atmospheres or combustible dusts. Additionally, pumping liquids with long fibers, liquids not compatible with the construction materials of the unit, and liquids with temperatures higher than the specified limits are considered improper use. Therefore, hazardous chemicals would include flammable, explosive, aggressive, toxic, corrosive liquids, and those not compatible with the pump materials or exceeding temperature limits as indicated in the technical information section. 4. Transport and storage
4.1 Delivery
The DMX 227 dosing pumps are supplied in different packaging,
depending on pump type and the overall delivery. For transport
and intermediate storage, use the correct packaging to protect
the pump against damage.
4.2 Intermediate storage
•
Permissible storage temperature: -20 °C to +50 °C.
•
Permissible air humidity: max. relative humidity: 92 %
(non-condensing).
4.3 Unpacking
Retain the packaging for future storage or return, or dispose of
the packaging in accordance with local regulations.
4.4 Return
Return the pump in its original packaging or equivalent.
The pump must be thoroughly cleaned before it is returned or
stored. It is essential that there are no traces of toxic or
hazardous media remaining on the pump.
Before returning the pump to Grundfos for service, the safety
declaration at the end of these instructions must be filled in by
authorised personnel and attached to the pump in a visible
position.
If Grundfos is requested to service the pump, it must be ensured
that the pump is free from substances that can be injurious to
health or toxic. If the pump has been used for such substances,
the pump must be cleaned before it is returned.
If proper cleaning is not possible, all relevant information about
the chemical must be provided.
If the above is not fulfilled, Grundfos can refuse to accept the
pump for service. Possible costs of returning the pump are paid
by the customer.

raw_model_output: The maximum operating pressure (maximum head) for DOC submersible pumps at 50 Hz frequency is 6.9 meters (23 feet) for the 3CG model and 11.1 meters (36 feet) for the 7CG and 7T models. For the DOC VX models, the maximum head is 7.2 meters (24 feet). At 60 Hz frequency, the maximum head is 6.8 meters (22 feet) for the 36CG model and 10.6 meters (35 feet) for the 76CG and 76T models, with 6.7 meters (22 feet) for the 76VXCG and 76VXT models. This information indicates the maximum pressure head the pump can handle during operation [Document 2, p.23].
returned_answer: The maximum operating pressure (maximum head) for DOC submersible pumps at 50 Hz frequency is 6.9 meters (23 feet) for the 3CG model and 11.1 meters (36 feet) for the 7CG and 7T models. At 60 Hz frequency, the maximum head is 6.8 meters (22 feet) for the 36CG model and 10.6 meters (35 feet) for the 76CG and 76T models, with 6.7 meters (22 feet) for the 76VXCG and 76VXT models. raw_model_output:
The installation requirements for the Lowara DOC pump include that all hydraulic and electrical connections must be completed by a technician possessing the technical-professional requirements outlined in the current regulations. Before starting work, it is necessary to check that the unit is unplugged and that the pump unit, the control panel, and the auxiliary control circuit cannot restart, even unintentionally. Additionally, the external protection conductor (ground) must always be connected to the ground terminal before attempting to make any other electrical connections to avoid electrical hazards [xylem_lowara_doc_iom_doc_submersible_pump_units_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=16|s=Page 16].

Regarding error code meanings, the Lowara DOC pump is equipped with self-diagnostics and malfunction detection. Defects detected by the pump system are signaled to the user with alternating short and long LED light flashes. The error codes and their meanings are as follows:

- Low voltage failure: Blinking 1 short – 1 long
- Overtemperature failure: Blinking 3 short – 1 long
- Speed feedback failure: Blinking 4 short – 1 long
- Blocked rotor: Blinking 5 short – 1 long

Normal operation is indicated by a continuous LED light on. The air purge sequence is indicated by blinking 200 ms on - 200 ms off - 200 ms on, and standby mode is indicated by blinking 50 ms on - 1.5 s off - 50 ms on. This self-diagnostic function may be switched off in some special OEM versions [xylem_bell_gossett_e3_4_e3_6_iom_series_e3_4_e3_6_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=38|s=Page 38].

Before starting work, it is necessary to check that the unit is unplugged and that the pump unit, the control panel, and the auxiliary control circuit cannot restart, even unintentionally. Additionally, the external protection conductor (ground) must always be connected to the ground terminal before attempting to make any other electrical connections to avoid electrical hazards [xylem_lowara_doc_iom_doc_submersible_pump_units_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=16|s=Page 16].

Regarding error code meanings, the Lowara DOC pump is equipped with self-diagnostics and malfunction detection. Defects detected by the pump system are signaled to the user with alternating short and long LED light flashes. The error codes and their meanings are as follows:

- Low voltage failure: Blinking 1 short – 1 long
- Overtemperature failure: Blinking 3 short – 1 long
- Speed feedback failure: Blinking 4 short – 1 long
- Blocked rotor: Blinking 5 short – 1 long

Normal operation is indicated by a continuous LED light on. The air purge sequence is indicated by blinking 200 ms on - 200 ms off - 200 ms on, and standby mode is indicated by blinking 50 ms on - 1.5 s off - 50 ms on. This self-diagnostic function may be switched off in some special OEM versions [xylem_bell_gossett_e3_4_e3_6_iom_series_e3_4_e3_6_installation_operation_and_maintenance_manual.pdf|p=38|s=Page 38].

3.6
Intended use
Circulating pump for domestic hot water systems.
If hot water is not used for longer periods of time, the water in the hot water pipe cools off.
Domestic hot water pumps (also called sanitary or drinking water circulating pumps) pump this
cold water back into the water heater via a separate recirculation pipe, or directly into the cold
water supply line (see Figure 5 and Figure 6 on page 19 and 20). At the same time fresh hot
water is flowing out of the water heater and provides a constant supply of hot water at the tap.
WARNING: Risk of electric shock
This pump has not been investigated for use in swimming pool or marine areas.
Do not install within an outer enclosure or beneath the skirt of a hot tub or spa.
This pump is not submersible.
CAUTION:
Acceptable for indoor use only. This pump has been evaluated for use with water only. Use with
maximum 203 °F (95 °C) water.
Pump selection
The e3-4 series models are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences with
a pipe loop (the total length of hot water supply line plus the recirculation line) up to 250 ft (76 m).
The e3-6 series pumps are designed to handle the recirculation requirements of residences and
small apartment complexes with pipe loop runs to 700-1000 ft (213-305 m).

raw_model_output:
If a Fleck 9000 water conditioner is not responding, the following troubleshooting steps should be taken:

1. Check if electrical service to the unit has been interrupted. Ensure permanent electrical service by checking the fuse, plug, pull chain, or switch.

2. Verify if the timer is defective. If so, replace the timer.

3. Confirm there has not been a power failure. If there was, reset the time of day.

4. Check if the bypass valve is open and close it if necessary.

5. Ensure there is salt in the brine tank and maintain the salt level above the water level.

6. Inspect and clean the injector screen if it is plugged.

7. Check the brine tank fill time and clean the brine line flow control if it is plugged.

8. If hardness is coming from the hot water tank, repeated flushings of the hot water tank may be required.

9. Inspect the distributor tube for leaks, cracks, and check the O-ring and tube pilot.

10. If there is an internal valve leak, replace seals, spacers, and/or piston.

11. Check for improper salt setting or excessive salt usage.

12. Investigate excessive water in the brine tank.

13. Check for loss of water pressure.

14. Clean iron buildup in the line to the water conditioner and inside the water conditioner itself. Add mineral cleaner to the mineral bed and increase regeneration frequency if needed.

15. Remove the piston and clean the control if the inlet is plugged due to foreign material.

16. Assure that the well system has a proper air eliminator control and check for dry well condition if there is loss of mineral through the drain line.

17. Verify the drain line flow control is properly sized.

These steps are summarized from the problem and correction table for water conditioner failure to regenerate in the Fleck 9000/9100/9500 Service Manual [pentair_fleck_9000_9100_9500_service_manual.pdf|p=37|s=Page 37].

Control Operation During Regeneration
During regeneration, the control shows the current
regeneration step number the valve is advancing to, or has
reached, and the time remaining in that step. The step number
that displays flashes until the valve completes driving to this
regeneration step position. Once all regeneration steps are
complete the valve returns to service and resumes normal
operation.
Pressing the Extra Cycle button during a regeneration cycle
immediately advances the valve to the next cycle step position
and resumes normal step timing.
Control Operation During Programming
The control only enters the Program Mode with the valve in
service. While in the Program Mode, the control continues
to operate normally monitoring water usage and keeping all
displays up to date. Control programming is stored in memory
permanently.
Manually Initiating a Regeneration
1.	 When the system is in service, press the Extra Cycle button
for five seconds on the main screen.
2.	 The control advances to Regeneration Cycle Step #1
(backwash), and begins programmed time count down.
3.	 Press the Extra Cycle button once to advance valve to
Regeneration Cycle Step #2 (brine draw and slow rinse).
4.	 Press the Extra Cycle button once to advance valve to
Regeneration Cycle Step #3 (rapid rinse).
5.	 Press the Extra Cycle button once to advance valve to
Regeneration Cycle Step #4 (brine refill).
6.	 Press the Extra Cycle button once more to advance the
valve back to in service.

Control Operation During a Power Failure
The SXT includes integral power backup. In the event of power
failure, the control shifts into a power-saving mode. The control
stops monitoring water usage. The display and motor shut
down, but it continues to keep track of the time and day for a
minimum of 8 hours.
The system configuration settings are stored in a non-volatile
memory and are stored indefinitely with or without power.
The Time of Day flashes when there has been a power failure.
Press any button to stop the Time of Day from flashing.
If power fails while the unit is in regeneration, the control will
save the current valve position before it shuts down. When
power is restored, the control will resume the regeneration
cycle from the point where power failed.
CAUTION  If power fails during a regeneration cycle, the valve
will remain in it’s current position until power
is restored. The valve system should include all
required safety components to prevent overflows
resulting from a power failure during regeneration.
The control will not start a new regeneration cycle without
power. If the valve misses a scheduled regeneration due to
a power failure, it will queue a regeneration. Once power is
